caption: Leaves display a dense, powdery white coating on their upper surfaces, forming a continuous, patchy, and irregular layer that gives a dusty or frosted appearance. No visible fruiting bodies are present.
Numerous tiny, dark, spherical heads are elevated on slender, hair-like stalks, scattered across the surface and resembling delicate pins emerging from the stem.

Small, black, roughly circular to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered and slightly raised on a pale, fibrous stem surface. The fruiting bodies have a matte to subtly textured appearance and are embedded or sitting atop the substrate.

Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly irregular structures are scattered densely across a pale, dry, and slightly textured surface. The black structures appear embedded or partially immersed, with no visible spore masses or color variation.

Small, dark, rounded bodies with fine, slender, translucent hair-like appendages extend outward. The structures are fuzzy and scattered, with appendages appearing slightly curved and emerging from a surface. The background is blurred, highlighting the distinct shapes and textures of the fungal bodies.

Leaves display a powdery white coating in diffuse, irregular patches, giving a dusty or floury appearance. The fungal growth is superficial and covers multiple leaves, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Several small, spherical bodies scattered on a fibrous surface; one is dark brown and opaque, while others are pale yellowish and translucent. Fine, hair-like filaments radiate from the smooth, rounded structures.

Greenish to olive-brown, foliose patches with rounded to irregular lobes and slightly wrinkled surfaces. Margins are crenate or lobulate, with scattered whitish or pale areas. Forms a patchy, contiguous mat on the bark.

Dense, powdery whitish mat with scattered, small, spherical fruiting bodies in reddish-brown and yellowish hues. Surface appears granular and filamentous, with fruiting bodies irregularly distributed across the field.

Small, dark, elongated to oval fruiting bodies embedded in a pale, roughened surface, surrounded by lighter, slightly raised patches and scattered black dots. The wood shows dry, cracked texture with some reddish-brown discoloration.

Convex cap with a greenish-yellow, slightly fibrillose surface. Gills beneath are pale lilac to light brown and closely spaced. Stout, yellowish stem with soil adhering and remnants of a web-like veil near the gills. Cap margin is smooth.

Tightly appressed, greenish to olive thallus with irregular, crenulate lobes and granular surface. Some paler or whitish patches are scattered throughout, and the overall texture appears uneven and slightly lobate.
Small, dark brown to black, lanceolate to irregularly shaped structures slightly raised above the bark, with a rough, granular, matte texture and scattered arrangement.
A dense, powdery white coating forms an irregular patch across the leaf surface, with a fine, granular texture that obscures much of the leaf’s natural color and venation.
Dense, powdery white growth covers the surface, dotted with numerous tiny, rounded structures ranging from pale yellow to dark brown, giving a granular, patchy appearance under magnification.

Minute, scattered, yellowish to ochre discs or cushions with granular surfaces and indistinct, slightly lobed margins. Fruiting bodies are closely grouped, some attached to fine, thread-like structures, and measure less than a millimeter in diameter.

Numerous small, black, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised above the dry, brown, fibrous wood surface, often surrounded by subtle discoloration or shallow depressions. No prominent external mycelium is visible.
Leaf surface covered with a dense, white, powdery coating forming a patchy, floury layer. The underlying green tissue is still visible in some areas, and no distinct fruiting bodies are present.

Numerous minute, rounded to slightly irregular ochre to yellowish fruiting bodies scattered across a dark surface, with fine whitish mycelial threads interspersed. The fruiting bodies are smooth, sessile, and clustered loosely, each less than a millimeter in diameter.
Pale, powdery, irregular pustules and swellings cover the stems and flower bases, forming granular, yellowish patches that slightly discolor and distort the plant tissue.
Small, yellow-orange, powdery spots scattered along the leaf veins, some slightly raised and surrounded by faint yellow halos, contrasting against the green leaf surface.

Numerous small, elongated, black, boat-shaped structures are scattered and clustered along the wood surface. These fruiting bodies are slightly raised, shiny, and embedded in the bark, forming linear to irregular patterns that follow the wood grain.

Green leaves display irregular, powdery white patches scattered across their surfaces. The white growth is fine and diffuse, forming patchy colonies. Some leaves show yellowing and minor necrosis near the affected areas.
Small, black, elongated and slightly raised structures are scattered along the dark brown twig, forming lance-shaped lesions or pustules embedded in the bark.

Numerous small, dark, rounded dots are scattered irregularly across the pale, fibrous stem surface. The dots are slightly raised and contrast with the parallel linear striations of the stem, appearing singly and in loose clusters.

Numerous small, elongated, black, and somewhat flattened fruiting bodies scattered across a woody surface. The fruiting bodies have a rough, irregular texture and vary slightly in size, appearing both solitary and in small clusters.

Numerous elongated, dark, boat-shaped to slit-like structures are embedded in the rough, brownish wood surface. The fruiting bodies are nearly black, slightly raised, and display central slits, with scattered greenish patches nearby.

Leaves display a patchy, powdery white coating on their upper surfaces, giving them a dull, grayish-white appearance. The fungal layer is diffuse and superficial, with some minor leaf damage and discoloration visible.
Dark, oval to elongated, slightly raised fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces and well-defined, lighter, sometimes reddish-brown margins, scattered and partially embedded in the woody bark.

Dense, intricate network of fine, hair-like filaments forming tangled coils and loops, interspersed with translucent, spherical bodies. The structures appear dark to translucent under magnification, creating an irregular, highly branched mesh.

Numerous small, elongated, black fruiting bodies with rough, slightly ridged surfaces are scattered and sometimes clustered on reddish-brown wood. The structures appear flattened, irregular, and often curved or boat-shaped, partially embedded in the bark.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded to irregular dots scattered across smooth, reddish-brown wood. Several pale, conical, feathery projections emerge from the surface, contrasting with the darker fruiting bodies.

Numerous tiny, black, dot-like fruiting bodies are scattered irregularly across smooth, light brown bark. The fruiting bodies are minute, circular to slightly oval, and embedded flush with the surface. A prominent, pointed woody protrusion is visible above the fruiting bodies.

Irregular, diffuse white powdery patches cover the upper surfaces of many green, serrated leaves. The thin, superficial fungal layer varies in density, leaving leaf veins visible and creating a mottled appearance against the glossy foliage.
Powdery white, web-like patches cover the leaf surface, dotted with numerous tiny, spherical structures in dark brown to black and yellowish hues, distributed along veins and interveinal areas.

Numerous small, pale, circular pustules are scattered across the green leaflets and stems, appearing slightly raised and whitish to cream. The infected areas look rougher than the smooth, uninfected foliage, with pustules concentrated along veins and midribs.

Numerous small, dark, slightly raised, irregularly shaped patches are embedded in a rough, fibrous surface. The dark structures are unevenly distributed, creating a mottled appearance against the lighter background.
Small brown fruiting bodies with wavy, striate caps and well-developed, radiating gills. The slender, slightly curved stipe is brown with soil remnants at the base. Cap surface appears matte and dry.

Leaf surface covered with dense, powdery, white to grayish patches forming a continuous, finely granular coating. The fungal growth appears as irregular blotches with diffuse margins blending into the green tissue beneath.

Numerous small, black, upright cylindrical to slightly curved structures emerge from a pale, wavy, and uneven surface. The black fruiting bodies have a rough texture, some with a slightly bulbous base, scattered irregularly across the cream-colored, coral-like background.
Irregular, patchy white powdery coating covers the upper surfaces of green leaves, forming diffuse spots and blotches. No visible fruiting bodies or discoloration beyond the white fungal patches.

Leaves display irregular, diffuse patches of white, powdery coating on their upper surfaces, giving a frosted, dusty appearance. Some leaf curling and minor damage are visible, but the main feature is the extensive white mycelial mat.
Branch surface shows rough, irregular, slightly swollen patches with dark, sunken spots and scattered tiny black dots embedded in the dry, cracked bark. Minor fissures and discoloration are visible.

Numerous tiny, black, oval to elongated fruiting bodies scattered irregularly on a pale, cracked woody surface. Each structure is slightly raised, embedded in the bark, and measures less than a millimeter across.
Small, whitish, powdery or pustular spots clustered along pale green stems and leaf petioles, appearing as minute, rounded, slightly raised groups on the plant surface.
Numerous small, pale yellow to whitish, circular pustules with central openings are scattered across the green, slightly swollen plant surface, giving a textured and dotted appearance.

Small, delicate fruiting bodies with convex to slightly flattened brownish-tan caps, some showing faint striations at the margins. Gills are brown and moderately spaced. Slender brown stems, often with soil clinging to the base, are visible. Some specimens are clustered.

Greenish to olive, irregularly shaped foliose thallus with flattened, wrinkled lobes. Surface appears granular and powdery in places, with uneven, lobulate margins and some lobes lifting from the substrate.

Small mushrooms with convex to irregularly wavy brown caps, rough textured surfaces, and slender brown stems. The gills underneath are well-developed, moderately spaced, and lighter brown, contrasting with the darker cap and stem.

Small, dark, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies embedded in bark, with rough, slightly raised surfaces and a few lighter patches. The structures appear scattered and are relatively small compared to the surrounding woody texture.
A green leaf with a serrated edge is covered by a white, powdery, and patchy coating forming irregular, diffuse patches that merge into a nearly continuous layer, especially along the veins.

White, crust-like layer tightly attached to wood, with a rough, uneven, granular surface. Scattered small, dark, upright structures emerge distinctly above the pale background, creating a striking contrast.

Robust mushrooms with convex to flattened, yellow-green to olive, sticky caps, some with soil debris. Stipes are thick, pale yellow to cream, with bulbous bases. Gills are lilac to pale purple and closely spaced. Cap margins are smooth.

Numerous small, scattered, orange-yellow pustules with a granular texture are visible on a green leaf surface. The pustules are slightly raised and irregularly distributed, concentrated near the leaf margin.
Numerous small, elongated, blackish fruiting bodies with rough, ridged surfaces and linear to slightly curved shapes are scattered irregularly across a light brown wood surface.
Numerous small, elongated, black, and somewhat flattened fruiting bodies scattered in irregular clusters on wood, with tough, dark, slightly shiny surfaces and well-defined margins.

Small fruiting bodies with convex to slightly flattened tan caps, dry matte surfaces, broad and spaced tan gills, and slender brownish cylindrical stipes with a slightly fibrous texture. Some soil particles adhere to the caps and stems.

Numerous small, pale yellow to whitish, round pustules are scattered and slightly raised along the length of the pale, discolored plant stems. The pustules are evenly spaced, with green leaves at the base remaining unaffected.

Small, clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened brown caps covered in fine fibrous scales. Gills are well-developed and lighter brown, radiating from slender, cylindrical, fibrous brown stems.

Leaves are coated with a dense, powdery white to grayish layer, forming a continuous, fine, granular mat that obscures the underlying leaf surface. The fungal growth appears evenly distributed, giving the leaves a frosted appearance.

Small, irregular yellowish-orange spots and slightly raised pustules scattered along the leaf veins, contrasting with the smooth, matte green surface and visible venation. The lesions are distinct and diagnostic, with no large spore masses present.

Numerous tiny, dark, spherical to slightly irregular heads are perched atop slender, upright, hair-like stalks. The heads appear dark brown to blackish, while the stalks are thin and paler. The structures are scattered across a fibrous, striated surface.

Numerous delicate, upright sporangia with slender, dark stalks and elongated, ragged brownish spore masses. The structures appear somewhat translucent and fibrous, scattered across the wood surface in small groups.
Numerous tiny, black, slightly raised dots scattered across pale grayish bark, some appearing embedded or just erupting through the surface. The bark also shows faint greenish and yellowish patches.
Numerous small, black, elongated to irregularly shaped fruiting bodies scattered and slightly raised on the wood surface, with a rough, uneven texture and embedded appearance.
Irregular, thin, whitish powdery patches scattered across the upper surface of a green leaf, giving a slightly fuzzy appearance without distinct fruiting bodies.

Patchy, contiguous mat of greenish to olive thallus tightly adhering to bark, composed of small, irregularly lobed segments with a granular, uneven surface and scattered lighter spots. Margins are irregular and blend into the substrate.

Small, yellowish to orange, circular to slightly irregular raised pustules densely scattered across green leaf surfaces. The pustules are numerous and distinct, forming clusters on both upper and lower sides of the leaves. The surrounding leaf tissue remains green and healthy-looking.

Faint, irregular, pale whitish to yellowish patches are visible along the midrib and veins of the green leaf, causing subtle discoloration and slight textural changes. No prominent fruiting bodies are present.
Small, nearly spherical black to dark brown fruiting bodies with rough surfaces, each surrounded by fine, radiating, hair-like appendages, are clustered on a green leaf with visible veins.

Green leaves display scattered, circular to irregular dark brown to purplish flat lesions, some with lighter centers and faint yellowish halos. Lesions vary in size and are smooth, with no visible raised structures or fruiting bodies.
A dense, powdery white mat covers the leaf, with numerous tiny, spherical structures in translucent white, yellow, and reddish-brown scattered across the web-like surface.

Numerous small, black, elongated to lance-shaped fruiting bodies are slightly raised and embedded in smooth reddish-brown bark, some with central openings. Scattered whitish patches are visible on the bark surface.

Elongated, dark brown to black, lance-shaped patches slightly raised above the bark surface, with a rough, granular texture and irregular distribution. Some patches are more oval, while others are distinctly elongated.

A fine, whitish to grayish powdery coating covers much of the elongated green leaf’s surface, appearing patchy and diffuse, especially in the central and basal areas. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

Numerous tiny, spherical structures ranging from reddish-brown to pale yellow, each with a slightly fuzzy surface and fine, radiating filaments. The spheres are closely grouped, with a delicate, hairy texture visible on their surfaces.

A dense, powdery, whitish to grayish mat covers the leaf surface, forming a fine, web-like texture that follows the veins. The growth appears felted and patchy, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible at this magnification.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped brown caps, some showing fine striations. One specimen displays widely spaced, radially arranged brown gills. Slender brown stems blend with the surrounding soil and plant debris.

Small brown mushrooms with convex to flat caps, distinctly striated and radially grooved margins, darker centers, and paler edges. Gills are broad, well-spaced, and wavy. Slender, cylindrical brown stems. Scattered among grass and clover.
Irregular, bright white, powdery patches scattered on the upper surface of green leaves. The colonies are diffuse, slightly raised, and sharply contrast with the healthy leaf tissue beneath.

Numerous tiny, spherical structures ranging from yellowish to reddish-brown, some translucent and others opaque, scattered and slightly clustered on a pale, fuzzy background. Surfaces appear smooth to subtly textured, with darker spheres grouped together.
A diffuse, irregular white powdery mat with a fine, web-like texture covers the leaf surface. Scattered small yellowish and reddish-brown spots are visible within the mycelial area.

Numerous small, dark, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered and partially embedded in a light woody surface, creating a speckled appearance. The fruiting bodies have a rough texture and lack prominent margins or visible spore masses.

A dark, nearly black, flattened and elongated structure with a rough, uneven surface and a distinct central groove. Margins are irregular and slightly raised, with the fruiting body partially immersed in the substrate.
Tiny, bright yellow-orange disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a granular surface, scattered on a dark shiny surface. Some display fine, hair-like structures around the edges.
Circular, powdery white patches with diffuse margins scattered across green leaf surfaces. The fungal growth appears thin, irregularly shaped, and superficial, lacking visible fruiting bodies.

Dark brown to nearly black, spherical structures with glossy surfaces, each fringed by fine, radiating, hair-like projections. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped, with a rough, spiny texture visible under magnification.
Small, pale, slightly raised pustules clustered on a green leaf, forming whitish to yellowish spots that subtly distort and discolor the leaf surface.

A mostly round, white structure partially buried in soil, with a smooth surface and some adhering dirt. A distinctive orange patch is visible on the upper part, hinting at the emerging cap beneath the enclosing veil.

Small, irregular, crust-like patches in pale greenish-gray cover the bark, displaying a granular to slightly warted texture with scattered, slightly raised circular structures. The surface appears uneven, with denser aggregations in some areas.

Elongated, black, narrow, boat-shaped structures scattered and clustered on the surface, slightly raised with rough, ridged texture and split or fissured margins. The fruiting bodies contrast against the woody, fibrous background.

Green leaves display irregular, white, powdery patches scattered across their surfaces. The fungal growth forms thin, diffuse layers, sometimes coalescing into larger spots, and appears superficial on the upper leaf surfaces.

Tightly attached, patchy mat with small, rounded to elongate olive-green lobes. Margins are slightly undulate or crenulate. Surface appears uneven, granular to slightly wrinkled, with a somewhat glossy look in places.

Bushy, upright plants with dense clusters of slender, needle-like leaves. Some leaf tips appear slightly yellowish or swollen, but no visible fruiting bodies or distinct fungal structures are present.

Textured, tan to light brown surface with scattered small, dark, circular to irregular embedded structures. The surface appears dry, slightly uneven, and features minute openings or ostioles, with subtle ridges and darker patches.

Numerous small, dark, slightly raised, irregular spots are scattered across a pale, textured surface. The spots have a rough, granular appearance and vary in size and shape, blending subtly into the background.

A densely packed layer of hyaline, thin-walled, polygonal to irregular cells with clear boundaries, forming a reticulate, textured surface. No visible pigmentation or reproductive structures are present.

Circular, white, powdery patches with dense, cottony texture and diffuse margins. Each patch has a central cluster of small, dark specks, standing out against the green leaf surface. Colonies are scattered and distinct.
Whitish, powdery patch forming an irregular, thin, diffuse layer on the green leaf surface. The fungal growth is fine-textured and contrasts with the healthy tissue, with no visible fruiting bodies.

Small, gregarious mushrooms with convex to slightly flattened, light brown to tan caps that appear dry and somewhat scaly. Gills are well-spaced and lighter brown, with slender, curved stipes matching the cap color and a paler base.

Small, rounded to irregular blackish fruiting bodies embedded in bark, some with star-like surface cracks. A few are slightly raised and show exposed dark interiors where the bark has split. Texture appears rough and scattered along the twig.

Numerous small, dark, slightly raised, irregularly shaped spots are scattered along the surface of a brown, elongated, and decaying plant fragment, with the substrate showing discoloration in tan and grayish hues.

A small, dark, roughly conical fruiting body with a granular texture, slightly raised above the wood surface. The margin is irregular and appears fused to the substrate, with no visible stipe or supporting structure.

Dark, crustose patches form irregular, thin, granular coverings on the stone. The surface is uneven and slightly rough, with a nearly black to dark brown color. Scattered minute yellow and orange dots are present, but the main focus is the patchy, discontinuous dark lichen.

Green leaves are covered with a conspicuous white to grayish powdery coating forming irregular patches. The thin, superficial layer gives the foliage a dull, dusty appearance, with fine, powdery mats visible on the upper leaf surfaces. No obvious leaf distortion is present.

Numerous tiny, reddish to orange pinhead-like structures densely clustered on a dark, moist, uneven surface. The fruiting bodies appear as scattered, minute dots, giving the area a speckled, textured appearance under magnification.
Layered, splintered wood with brown and gray hues, featuring fine granular and powdery deposits scattered across the fibrous surface, suggesting subtle fungal colonization.

A dense, white, powdery coating covers the green, lobed leaves and flower buds, with visible curling and distortion of the foliage. The powdery layer is most prominent along the leaf surfaces and stems.
Small, round cap with pronounced pleats and a scalloped edge. The center is a darker brown, fading to a pale grayish margin. The cap appears thin, delicate, and almost translucent.

Small, dark, disc-shaped to slightly cup-like fruiting bodies scattered and clustered on bark. They appear blackish to dark brown with irregular, slightly raised margins and central depressions. The surface is matte and somewhat rough, standing out against the lighter bark.

Leaf surface displays numerous circular to irregular pale-centered spots with dark reddish-brown margins. Some lesions merge into larger necrotic patches. Surrounding tissue shows yellowing and browning. No visible fruiting bodies. Serrated leaf edge and prominent veins are visible.

Small, delicate mushrooms with thin, translucent caps featuring pronounced radial striations and a slightly darker central disc. One cap displays a pleated, circular margin from above, while the other reveals closely spaced, pale gills beneath. Slender, smooth, pale stipes are visible.

Dense, powdery white mycelial growth covers the green leaf surface, with fine, filamentous hyphae forming a web-like mat. A small, dark, spherical structure is visible amid the cottony, patchy fungal layer.
Dense clusters of minute, globose to ovoid bodies with a pale grayish-blue, finely textured or frosted surface, forming a compact, granular mat directly on the substrate.
Numerous small, rust-brown, powdery pustules are scattered and slightly raised on the green leaf surface, with some forming small clusters. The pustules vary in size and are irregularly distributed.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies densely scattered across pale, weathered wood, appearing as minute, dark, slightly raised dots contrasting with the lighter background.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, moist, purplish-brown convex to flattened caps. Gills are closely spaced, broad, and lilac to brownish. Cylindrical stipes are pale lilac to whitish, often with soil at the base. Caps show even margins and various stages of development.

Elongated, brown, dried leaf segments with scattered, small, irregularly angular, pale to whitish fungal structures slightly raised and embedded along the darkened surface, contrasting with the rough, desiccated background.

A tiny, delicate, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, regular margin and pale cream to off-white color. The surface is finely textured and slightly translucent, supported by a short, slender stalk attached to a brown substrate.

Dense, irregular, crust-like mat with dark reddish-brown coloration. Surface is rough and uneven, featuring numerous small, clustered, cylindrical or tufted structures, giving a fibrous and compact appearance.

Two tiny, delicate fruiting bodies with smooth, whitish, disc- to cup-shaped caps and fine, even margins. The slender, translucent to pale brown stipes are slightly curved, attaching the velvety caps directly to the substrate.
Tiny, cream to pale yellow disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and slightly irregular edges, scattered and clustered on a dead stem. Fine, thread-like hyphae connect some of the discs.

Dense clusters of upright, elongated, dark bluish to purplish structures, each tipped with tiny, bright red spherical dots. The overall texture is fibrous and bristly, with the fruiting bodies closely packed together in a tufted arrangement.
Numerous small, rust-colored, slightly raised pustules scattered irregularly across elongated green leaves, with some leaf discoloration and damage visible around the infection sites.
Numerous tiny, rounded, whitish to pale gray bead-like structures densely cluster in linear and patchy patterns along green grass stems, giving a granular texture to the affected areas.
A minute, rounded fruiting body with a glossy, translucent surface and a central opening. The sporocarp is solitary, slightly raised, and set against a finely granular, brown background.
Densely clustered, small, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies with a pale grayish to whitish, powdery surface. Some show darker centers, and all are sessile, closely packed in a patchy arrangement.

Numerous small, black, roughly spherical to slightly elongated bumps with short, bristle-like projections are scattered irregularly across a pale, dry, fibrous surface. The dark fruiting bodies are slightly raised and have a rough texture, contrasting with the tan background.
Broad, yellow-ochre cap with a sticky, moist surface and a shallow central depression. The margin is slightly inrolled, and the cap is scattered with small bits of debris and darker spots.

Small, rust-brown, circular to irregular powdery pustules scattered on a green, hairy surface. The pustules are granular in texture and surrounded by fine, translucent hairs, appearing grouped but not merging.

A small, irregularly shaped, dark fungal colony less than 2 mm wide, densely covered with fine, silvery to blackish hair-like structures. The surface appears fuzzy and matted, slightly raised above the greenish-yellow substrate.

Dense, mat-like patch of minute, dark brown to nearly black bristly structures, scattered with tiny, vivid red dots. The surface appears fuzzy and slightly glossy, with the red dots providing a striking contrast against the dark background. Scale shows the fruiting bodies are very small.

Numerous small, black, hemispherical to slightly conical fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a woody surface, some partially embedded. The surrounding wood shows yellowish and reddish-brown discoloration. The fruiting bodies have a matte, slightly rough texture and vary slightly in size.

Dense, irregular dark reddish-brown patch forming a continuous, fuzzy to granular band along the wood. The margin is uneven and diffuse, blending gradually into the surface, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Tiny, white, dome-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and short, translucent stalks, scattered along a slender dark substrate. The margins are even and unornamented, and the overall appearance is delicate and minute.
Fine, powdery, whitish to off-white coating scattered in granular patches and thin mats on the leaf surface, with some denser, crystalline areas and occasional brownish spots.

Multiple circular to irregular spots with dark brown to purplish margins and pale, grayish, slightly raised centers scattered across a green leaf. Lesion centers appear textured, and surrounding leaf tissue shows yellowing and wrinkling.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded to slightly elongated bumps scattered across light brown, weathered wood. The dark fruiting bodies are embedded or partially immersed, giving a rough, slightly raised texture against the contrasting background.

Large mushroom with a yellowish, wavy cap margin, closely spaced pale yellow gills, and a thick, granular yellow stipe. The gills are decurrent, running slightly down the stipe. Soil clings to the robust base.
A faint, patchy white powdery film is visible on the upper surfaces of two elongated green leaves, creating a subtle, irregular discoloration without distinct fruiting bodies.

Leaf surface densely covered with small, round, reddish-brown, slightly raised pustules. Spots are irregularly distributed, with some merging into larger patches, especially along the veins. Surrounding tissue shows yellowing and browning.

Thin, white, irregularly branched vein-like networks with a granular, powdery surface spread delicately across green grass blades. The margins are uneven and diffuse, blending into the surrounding vegetation.
Leaves display scattered, small, dark brown to black raised pustules and spots. Some leaves show yellowing and necrotic patches, with the pustules irregularly distributed across the foliage.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, slightly raised pustules scattered across green leaf surfaces, often concentrated along veins and margins. Some leaf edges show minor tears and discoloration near the pustules.

Numerous tiny, bright red to orange, spherical to slightly oval dots densely speckle the rough, dark brown, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies appear partially embedded, creating a fine, vivid pattern against the uneven substrate.

Sectioned fruiting body with a smooth, moist pinkish-brown cap and closely spaced, pale pinkish-brown gills. The solid stipe is fibrous and matches the cap in color. Gills appear slightly serrated at the edges.

A delicate, slender mushroom with a long, thin white stem and a small, pale brown cap. The cap is semi-translucent with pronounced radial striations and free, closely spaced gills visible underneath. Cap diameter is less than 2 cm.
Leaves are coated with a dense, powdery white layer forming irregular patches. The white covering gives a frosted, dusty appearance, while leaf veins remain visible beneath the even fungal mat.

A dense layer of tiny, spherical, grayish-white fruiting bodies closely packed together, forming a granular, powdery patch on the surface of a brown, dried leaf. The sporangia are uniform in size and appear smooth and sessile.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies densely scattered across a brown, dead stem. The discs are minute, smooth, and rounded, appearing directly attached to the surface without visible stalks.

Mature fruiting body with a brown, wrinkled cap and densely packed, broad gills in a pinkish-lilac brown shade. The pale, fibrous stem shows soil at the base. Cap margin is slightly wavy. One specimen displays the gills, another the textured cap surface.

A circular, grayish patch with a dense, felt-like, woolly texture sits on a yellow-brown leaf. The lesion is slightly raised with a distinct, subtly dark border separating it from the surrounding healthy tissue.
A small, circular cap with pronounced radial grooves and a slightly darker center sits atop a long, slender, translucent stipe. The cap appears deeply pleated, thin, and fragile.

Numerous small, dark, nearly black, rounded to slightly flattened fruiting bodies densely clustered together. Surfaces appear rough and minutely hairy, forming a contiguous mat with a granular texture. Some areas show a greenish tinge.

A tiny, brown, globose fruiting body with a slightly roughened surface, perched singly on fibrous, moist wood. The fruiting body appears subtly textured and is distinctly separate from the surrounding substrate.
Whitish, powdery web-like growth covers the leaf surface, dotted with small, dark, spherical bodies bearing fine, radiating appendages. Minute yellowish spheres are scattered among the network.

Several minute, black, rounded to slightly domed structures are scattered across a pale, woody surface. These smooth, dark fruiting bodies are partially embedded and contrast sharply with the lighter background, appearing isolated rather than clustered.
Numerous small, pale grayish-white, globose to slightly elongated structures densely clustered in a line along a green stem, with a granular, powdery surface and smooth margins.

Tiny, whitish to pale cream cup-shaped structures with a slightly granular surface, closely attached and clustered together. Some have scalloped or irregular margins, and all appear minute and delicate against the background.

Tiny, white, smooth disc-shaped fruiting bodies with slightly convex to flat surfaces, scattered along thin brown plant debris. The apothecia are minute, delicate, and appear nearly sessile or with very short stalks.

Small, rounded, densely clustered structures with a powdery, granular surface and pale grayish coloration, forming irregular compact masses. The fine surface detail and tight arrangement of the bodies are clearly visible.

Multiple circular to oval spots with brownish, slightly sunken centers and darker, well-defined margins scattered across a yellowed leaf. Lesions vary in size, some coalescing, with textured centers indicating sporulation.

Numerous small, rounded to irregular, slightly raised dull greenish-gray patches scattered across a brownish-orange leaf surface. The patches have a granular texture and are irregularly distributed, interrupting the smooth, fibrous leaf with clustered and isolated spots.
Delicate, bright white, bead-like masses form linear or slightly branched clusters along grass blades. The structures appear powdery to granular, standing out against the green and yellow grass.

Numerous tiny, bright red, globose to slightly elongated fruiting bodies are scattered in small clusters across a dark, fibrous, layered background. The fruiting bodies are smooth, moist, and distinctly colored, standing out sharply against the brownish substrate.

Elongated, brown, dried needles display scattered, small, dark, circular to irregular spots. The spots are slightly raised and distributed across the needle surface, with surrounding tissue faintly discolored. The needles appear dry and papery, with minute dot-like fungal structures visible.
Small, dark, irregularly shaped fruiting bodies with rough, textured surfaces are scattered and partially embedded in weathered, decaying wood among tangled branches.

A tiny, delicate fungus with a smooth, white, hemispherical cap and a slender, translucent to whitish, finely textured stem. The cap margin is even and unlobed. Another blurred fruiting body appears in the background.

Numerous small, pale grayish to whitish, globose fruiting bodies with a powdery surface are densely clustered along a thin green structure, each appearing uniform in size and closely packed, highlighted against a dark background.

Minute, nearly circular fruiting body with a shiny, dark brown to black surface. The peridium is thick, rigid, and displays a distinctive, irregularly polygonal cracked pattern. Texture is smooth and glossy, and the structure is solitary and less than 1 mm in diameter.

Grass blades are densely coated with tiny, rounded, whitish to pale gray granules forming a powdery, frosted layer. The granules are closely packed and evenly distributed along the stems, giving a granular appearance.
Tiny, bright yellow, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces and even margins, scattered and occasionally clustered along the plant stem.
Cluster of mushrooms with convex, purplish-brown caps and inrolled, uneven margins. Gills are closely spaced and purplish, while the pale stipes show fibrous texture and soil remnants at the base.
Numerous tiny, rounded, pale to whitish dots scattered across moist, dark brown wood. The fruiting bodies are minute, globose, smooth, and slightly raised, loosely grouped but not densely clustered.
