Dry, brown conifer needles with numerous tiny, black, dot-like fruiting bodies scattered irregularly along their surfaces. The dark specks are slightly raised and embedded in the needle tissue, contrasting with the fibrous texture.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly sunken in the rough woody surface, with a patchy greenish covering nearby. The apothecia have a rough texture and indistinct margins.

Bright yellow-orange fruiting body with a wavy, irregularly lobed cap margin. Well-developed, decurrent gills radiate from a short, pale stipe. The surface appears smooth and moist, and the mushroom is small and delicate.
Tiny, black, spherical structures scattered on a glossy green leaf surface; each fruiting body is slightly raised and smooth, standing out against the fine surface hairs of the leaf.

Small, delicate mushroom with a gray, radially grooved cap and slightly upturned, fragile margin. The cap appears translucent and finely striate, supported by a slender, pale stem emerging from sandy ground.
A delicate mushroom with a dark gray, pleated cap showing irregular splits at the margin, supported by a slender, smooth, pale stipe rising from sandy ground.

Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly irregular dots are scattered densely across the pale, smooth bark. The dots are slightly raised, some with tiny central openings, and are embedded in the surface. The bark shows mild discoloration and cracking.

Green leaves display a conspicuous whitish, powdery coating forming diffuse, irregular patches on the upper surfaces. The powdery areas contrast with the natural green of the broad, oval leaves, giving a frosted appearance.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to blackish, disc-like fruiting bodies scattered across the bark, appearing as slightly raised, rounded patches with a granular texture. Some yellow-greenish patches are also present, but the dark discs are distinct and closely appressed to the surface.

Broad, nearly flat caps with a smooth, matte surface and rich yellow to ochre color. Margins are slightly wavy and irregular, with minor notches and cracks. Caps are medium-sized and clustered, with a dry appearance and some debris on the surface.

Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly elongated dots scattered irregularly across rough, light brown bark. The dark spots are slightly raised or immersed, giving the surface a finely dotted appearance. No other visible structures.

A dense, powdery white to grayish coating covers much of the green, deeply lobed leaf, forming a fine, dusty mat that obscures the leaf’s natural texture. The fungal growth appears patchy but extensive across the surface.

Dark, roughly spherical to irregular clusters with diffuse margins are embedded in a yellowish-brown matrix. Numerous small, rounded elements surround the main dense, granular structures, which range from dark brown to black against a lighter background.
Small, diffuse olive-brown to dark greenish tufts scattered across a pale, striated surface. The minute colonies appear fuzzy or powdery with an irregular, granular texture and lack distinct margins.

Cross-section of decayed wood with a hollow, fibrous center and dark, encrusted patches on the outer bark, suggesting fungal presence. The wood appears pale and brittle with irregular, darkened margins.
A dense, white, powdery coating covers the leaf surface, forming a continuous, fine, and evenly distributed layer that gives the leaf a frosted appearance. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Numerous small, raised, yellowish to brown pustules cover the stem, appearing slightly elongated and irregular with a rough texture. The pustules are distributed along the surface, standing out against the smooth background.

A small, cushion-like, pale to dark brown fruiting body protrudes from the bark, with a roughened surface and a distinct central opening. The surrounding bark is slightly lifted and discolored near the structure.

Green leaves display numerous small, circular to irregular pale spots, many with darker centers and faint yellowish halos, scattered across the surfaces. The lesions vary in size and are distributed on multiple leaves.

A single, slender, club-shaped structure with a curved apex and slightly swollen base. The surface is finely textured and appears somewhat hairy, with pale coloration and a darker margin outlining the elongated, delicate form.

Numerous small, dark, conical to globose structures scattered across a fibrous, granular surface, interspersed with fine, whitish mycelial threads. The coloration ranges from dark brown and black to lighter tan, with occasional white patches.

Dense, dark black central mass with irregular, diffuse margins. Edges appear woolly or filamentous, transitioning to lighter brown and tan hues with a granular or fibrous texture. No distinct fruiting bodies visible.
Dark, irregular, powdery or crust-like patches form a continuous band along the swollen, discolored stem, with some yellowish or pale margins visible against the plant tissue.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, slightly raised pustules scattered irregularly across the green leaf surface, with yellowing around the infection sites. The pustules break through the leaf epidermis.

Several minute, slender, coral-pink to pale orange, club-shaped or slightly curved fruiting bodies emerge sparsely from the plant stem surface. The fruiting bodies are delicate, smooth, and lack a distinct cap or gills.
The green, lobed leaf is covered with numerous small, round to slightly irregular yellowish-orange spots densely scattered across the surface, especially along the veins and between them.

Several dark, smooth, ellipsoid to slightly ovoid spores are clustered together, each with uniform coloration. The background consists of translucent, septate hyphal tissue, highlighting the spores' distinct outlines under microscopic view.

Numerous small, dark, circular to oval fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on light brown bark, each surrounded by a faint greenish halo. The bark surface is textured with irregular green patches.

Large, irregular, dark brown to blackish mass with a velvety, granular surface. The fruiting body is flat, spread out, and measures about 10–12 cm long, with diffuse margins blending into the decaying wood substrate.
A dense mat of minute, bright yellow, rounded granules tightly packed together, forming a rough, powdery, and vivid yellow crust across the surface with no distinct margin.
Numerous small, dark, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on moist brown bark, each with a rough texture and punctate appearance.

Translucent, cup-shaped structure with a smooth, moist surface and slightly undulating margin. Fine, hair-like projections line the upper edge. The body is mostly pale, with subtle yellowish and greenish tones in the surrounding area.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, smooth brownish-tan caps, closely spaced pale gills, and pale cylindrical stems showing brownish streaks. Soil and leaf litter cling to the bases.

Numerous small, rust-colored, slightly raised pustules are scattered irregularly across the undersides of green, hairy leaves. The pustules vary in size and density, with some leaf distortion and discoloration visible.

Green leaves display scattered, irregular brown circular spots with slightly sunken centers and faint yellowish halos. Leaf edges are uneven and show signs of decay. Lesions vary in size and are prominent against the green background.
A small, cylindrical to rounded fruiting body with a bright orange to reddish-orange cap, densely covered in fine, whitish fibrils or scales near the base, giving it a velvety appearance.

Small, clustered, rust-brown pustules with a powdery, granular texture are slightly raised above the green leaf surface, forming irregular groups. Fine leaf hairs and the leaf’s surface texture are clearly visible around the pustules.

Densely packed, irregular, layered surface with pinkish to light tan coloration. Spongy, porous texture featuring numerous maze-like, angular pores. Fruiting body spreads flatly, with some darker, moist patches and an indistinct, irregular margin.

Cluster of slender mushrooms with convex to slightly umbonate, pale brown to tan velvety caps. Gills are crowded and pale to medium brown. Stipes are long, thin, whitish to pale brown, and fibrous, with some surface fibrils visible.

Patchy, crust-like mat with a grayish-brown color and felted, fibrous texture. Surface appears uneven and granular, with some areas showing a denser, woolly or hairy margin, closely adhering to the wood.

Whitish to pale gray, crust-like patches with a cracked, areolate surface. The margins are irregular and blend into the substrate. The surface appears dry, rough, and uneven, lacking any distinct cap, stem, or gills.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded to slightly elongated fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on rough, mottled bark with greenish patches. Some fruiting bodies display a central opening.

Slender, pale stem supporting a small, conical to cylindrical cap with pronounced vertical grooves. The cap surface is pale with subtle brownish tinges near the apex and an even, non-deliquescent margin. Texture appears slightly fibrous throughout.

Rust-colored, fuzzy patches with a granular texture form irregular, linear bands along green plant tissue. The brownish growth has diffuse margins blending into the substrate, and appears powdery under high magnification.

Dense patches of bright yellow, finely granular crust cover the surface, forming irregular, tightly packed clusters. The granules are small, rounded, and give a rough, powdery texture without visible large fruiting bodies.

Irregular, crust-like masses with pale beige to light brown coloration. The surface is rough, uneven, and cracked, displaying a wavy, lobed margin. The structure appears resupinate and closely attached, with a slightly fibrous or granular texture.

Small, irregular, brown to dark brown structures with a rough, warty texture emerge in clusters from a woody surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded, with uneven margins and a slightly reddish, yellowish background.

Small, dark brown to black, irregularly shaped, warty fruiting bodies clustered and slightly raised along a woody twig, appearing embedded or erupting from the bark. The stromata are scattered to grouped, with a rough texture and no visible spore masses.

Numerous dark, irregularly shaped, crust-like pustules densely scattered across the leaf surface, forming rough, raised patches that coalesce and cause visible deformation and discoloration of the leaf tissue.

Clustered, irregularly shaped, dark brown to blackish structures with a rough, warty, crust-like texture emerge from a reddish-brown woody surface. The fruiting bodies are scattered and partially embedded, lacking visible stalks or caps.

Pinkish to pale salmon, irregular patches with a fibrous, rough texture. Surface appears cracked in places with darker brown discolorations and uneven, slightly fimbriate margins. Some areas show denser, tufted growth.
Small, scattered, dark olive to brownish fuzzy patches form minute, irregular colonies with a velvety or granular texture on the striated stem surface.
Scattered, rust-brown, powdery pustules and irregular aggregations form circular and patchy clusters on the green leaf surface, with a granular texture and some surrounding yellow discoloration.
Multiple circular, slightly sunken lesions with brown, roughened centers and defined margins are scattered across the dark, smooth fruit surface. The lesions appear dry and crusty.

Several small, circular, dark brown to blackish spots are scattered on a pale yellow-green surface. A reddish-brown, curved structure with a granular texture is visible at the edge. The surface appears rough and uneven under high magnification.
A single, translucent, ellipsoid spore with a clear central septum is visible, appearing smooth and hyaline against a pale, slightly granular background under the microscope.

Extensive, tightly-adhering patches with a pinkish to salmon hue, covered in dense, short, irregular maze-like ridges and pores. The surface appears rough and fibrous, with diffuse margins blending gradually into the wood substrate.

Large, irregular, blackish to dark brown mass with a granular, velvety surface. Amorphous and closely appressed to the wood, lacking distinct stalks or individual fruiting bodies. Surface is uneven with minor fissures.
Small, elongated, blackish structures slightly raised and embedded in the wood surface, appearing smooth and arranged in parallel or scattered lines, contrasting with the lighter wood background.

Large, irregular, cushion-like black mass with a finely granular to velvety surface. Scattered lighter patches and granules are visible, and the margin blends diffusely into the wood. No distinct stalks or individual fruiting bodies are present.

Small, irregular dark openings break through the bark, each surrounded by slightly raised, discolored, rough patches. The ostioles are scattered in a linear pattern along the woody surface, with brown and tan hues dominating the scene.
No visible fungal structures are present; only green herbaceous plants with small white flowers and slender stems are seen. The image is slightly out of focus, obscuring fine details.

Numerous tiny, pale whitish to yellowish patches scattered across a reddish-brown, cracked surface. The fungal growth appears as minute, irregularly shaped colonies, giving the area a fine, patchy texture with no prominent fruiting bodies visible.

Irregular, cushion-like white mass with a bumpy, granular surface, spreading across decaying wood. The surface appears moist and slightly glistening, with no distinct stalks or individual fruiting bodies visible.
Numerous small, round, yellow-orange pustules densely scattered and slightly raised on the green leaf underside, often aligned along the veins. The leaf has a lobed margin and prominent venation.
Small, rounded cap with pronounced striations and a dry, fibrous surface. The cap is orange-brown, with an even margin. The slender, pale stipe is mostly hidden from view.

Several elongated, oval-shaped structures with granular internal contents are scattered across a yellowish, translucent background. The structures have smooth, clearly defined edges and are evenly dispersed in the microscopic field.

Dark, irregularly shaped, granular fungal mass with dense, matted texture and fibrous margins. Numerous fine, hair-like hyphae radiate outward. Several oval, darkly pigmented spores are scattered around the main cluster. Overall coloration is dark brown to black.

Extensive, irregular, crust-like patch with pale pinkish to salmon coloration, uneven and granular surface, and indistinct margins blending into moss-covered wood. No cap or stem structures are visible; the fungus spreads patchily over the substrate.

Dark, irregular patches embedded in bark, featuring several circular, slightly raised structures with central openings. The surface is rough, cracked, and dark brown to black, contrasting with lighter, green-mossed bark. Margins are irregular and diffuse.

Bright yellow, finely granular crust forming dense, irregular patches closely adhering to rough bark. The surface is powdery with numerous tiny, rounded yellow structures densely packed together. Margins are diffuse, blending gradually into the substrate without a distinct border.

Elongated, narrow, blackish fruiting bodies slightly raised and embedded in the wood surface, appearing linear to slightly curved with smooth, dark exteriors that blend subtly into the lighter, fibrous substrate.

Cluster of small, cup-like discs with yellow-orange centers and pale, slightly raised margins. Surfaces are granular and uneven, with dark speckling on the discs. The arrangement is dense and overlapping, with rough texture and dominant yellow-green hues.

Dense, irregular blackish mat with a velvety to finely granular surface, appearing cushion-like and matte. The margin is diffuse, blending into the wood substrate. No distinct individual fruiting bodies are visible at this scale.

Thin, patchy, crust-like layer with a matte, velvety surface and irregular margins. Coloration is dark brown to grayish, blending into decaying wood. Surface appears uneven and slightly fuzzy in some areas.

Irregular, rust-brown to reddish patches with granular, slightly roughened surfaces and diffuse margins. The patches are slightly raised, with a subtle yellowish halo and uneven coloration, ranging from lighter to darker reddish-brown, showing granular or powdery areas.

Small, dark, nearly spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a rough, granular surface, scattered among bright green moss. The fruiting bodies are sessile and contrast sharply with the surrounding vegetation.

Dense, powdery white coating forming irregular patches and spots on green leaf surfaces, creating a mottled appearance. The fungal growth is superficial and distinctly powdery, with no visible fruiting bodies.
Small, clustered, black, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies with a smooth, slightly shiny surface, tightly grouped within bark crevices and surrounded by peeling bark fragments.

Extensive, crust-like patches tightly adhere to the wood, displaying pale pinkish to cream tones with an uneven, wavy, and cracked surface. The margin is diffuse and irregular, blending gradually into the substrate.

Dense, irregular, spongy surface with a pinkish to salmon hue. The texture is maze-like with angular, labyrinthine pores and an uneven, slightly lobed margin. Crust-like and tightly attached, with scattered plant debris visible.
Green leaves with fine, short, white hairs along the margins and surfaces, giving a soft, slightly velvety appearance. No visible fungal structures or discoloration present.
Slender, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a pale whitish to pinkish hue and smooth, slightly granular surface. Small and delicate, they emerge singly and are spaced apart.

Numerous small, rounded to slightly irregular brownish apothecia with a granular surface are scattered across a thin, pale, granular crust, closely interspersed among green moss leaves. The apothecia are sessile and vary slightly in size, forming patchy groupings.

Surface densely covered with small, rounded, brown to dark brown granules forming clustered, uneven, powdery patches. The texture appears granular and crust-like, with subtle variations in color and no visible stalks or prominent fruiting bodies.

Numerous small, black, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies are closely grouped and slightly elevated, each covered with fine, hair-like filaments, giving a fuzzy appearance above the fibrous substrate.
Small, black, roughly circular to irregular fruiting bodies scattered on bark, slightly raised or embedded, with a shiny, hard, crust-like texture and indistinct margins blending into the wood.

Small, circular to irregular brown lesions with slightly raised margins and darker centers are scattered across the green leaf, each surrounded by lighter halos. The leaf also shows some marginal damage and discoloration.
Leaves are covered with a dense, powdery white coating forming irregular silvery patches, giving the foliage a whitish, dusted appearance while underlying green tissue remains visible.
Minute, scattered, fuzzy olive-brown to dark brown patches with a velvety, cushion-like appearance. The colonies are low, irregular, and powdery, forming small, isolated groups on a fibrous surface.

Green, lance-shaped leaves display scattered, small, dark brown to black, slightly raised pustules. Some leaves show yellowish discoloration around the spots, with the rest of the foliage appearing healthy.

Small, shiny black globose fruiting bodies emerge from bark fissures on a discolored, roughened woody surface. The bark is cracked and slightly raised around the fungal structures, highlighting their embedded appearance.

Small, irregular, pale crust-like patches slightly raised above the bark, with rough, granular surfaces and uneven, cracked margins. Minute, darker depressions are visible, blending subtly into the light brown woody substrate.

Dark, rough surface with scattered yellow-greenish mottling and lighter patches. The texture is uneven with small cracks and irregularities, lacking distinct fruiting bodies. Predominantly dark brown to black coloration.
Dark, irregular, crust-like patch with a powdery, granular texture on a green plant stem. The affected area appears roughened and contrasts with the smooth, healthy stem nearby.

Numerous tiny, rounded to slightly irregular, pale brown to grayish disk-like fruiting bodies are scattered across vibrant green moss. The apothecia are flat to slightly convex, smooth-margined, somewhat translucent, and lack visible stalks, blending subtly with the mossy background.

Small, dark brown to black, irregularly shaped pustules breaking through the green stem, each surrounded by a faint yellowish halo. The pustules are slightly raised and have a rough, granular surface.
Clusters of round to oval, rust-colored pustules with a granular, powdery texture and diffuse margins scattered across a greenish surface.

Small, rounded, tan to light brown structures with irregular margins, each dotted with prominent black spots. The fruiting bodies are scattered and partially embedded in the woody surface, with a rough texture from the black dots.

Bright yellow to orange-yellow crust forming irregular, patchy layers with a cracked, granular to areolate texture. Surface appears uneven with small, tightly packed granules blending into the wood substrate.
Layered, shelf-like fruiting bodies with wavy, irregular, and lobed margins. The surface is pale to light brown, rough, and cracked, forming effused-reflexed patches distinct from surrounding moss.

A small, circular, slightly raised brownish lesion with a darker center and lighter margin on a green leaf. The lesion appears rougher than the surrounding tissue, with additional tiny scattered spots nearby.

Broad green leaves display numerous pale yellow, angular to irregular spots with diffuse margins. The discoloration appears between leaf veins, creating a mottled pattern. Leaf edges are serrated and surfaces slightly rough. No visible fruiting bodies.

Woody surface with scattered, small, rounded, raised structures, some with dark circular openings. The texture is rough and cracked, with greenish and brownish coloration. Structures appear slightly embedded and irregularly distributed.

Delicate, radiating, multi-lobed structures with elongated, lanceolate appendages and a finely filamentous, feathery texture. Numerous dark, oval to ellipsoid spores are scattered and clustered around the structures on a pale, translucent background with visible air bubbles.

Oval to bell-shaped cap with pronounced grooves and fine, hair-like structures. The surface shows pale brown and subtle reddish hues with some darker specks. A slender stem is partially visible. Image is dimly lit, obscuring finer details.
Minute, rounded disc-like fruiting body with a smooth, pale beige surface and slightly translucent appearance, set among bright green moss leaves and a whitish, granular background.

Small, black, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies clustered on a discolored, reddish-brown patch of bark. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised with a glossy surface, contrasting against the surrounding bark and yellowish-green patches.
Small, irregular dark brown to rust-colored pustules clustered on a green leaf, each surrounded by a pale, slightly yellowish halo where the leaf tissue is discolored.

Small, rounded, translucent to whitish fruiting bodies with a gelatinous, moist appearance emerge from a brown, irregularly textured surface. The fruiting bodies are closely grouped, smooth-margined, and lack visible stalks or gills.

Numerous small, dark, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies densely clustered, each covered with fine, hair-like setae giving a fuzzy texture. The coloration is predominantly dark brown to black, with lighter tan to beige material interspersed. No distinct stipes are visible.

Slender, elongated, pale structures with a smooth surface, sparsely scattered and slightly raised from thin plant stems. The minute, club-shaped fruiting bodies are only a few millimeters long and appear delicate under magnification.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, convex to hemispherical caps in purplish to violet tones, some showing faint cracks. Thick, robust stipes display remnants of a web-like veil. Gills are pale to grayish beneath moist, slightly sticky caps.

Numerous small, dark, rounded to slightly elongated bumps are scattered irregularly across a light brown, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded and barely protrude, giving a speckled appearance to the substrate.
Minute, scattered dark brown to blackish pustules and a single orange-brown powdery spore mass on a finely hairy, veined leaf underside. Pustules are slightly raised and irregularly grouped.

A green surface densely coated with a fine, powdery, whitish layer. The growth appears diffuse and patchy, with some areas showing slightly denser, powdery aggregations. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Dense clusters of small, yellow to yellow-green, irregularly shaped structures with a granular, slightly lobed texture. The surface appears uneven and powdery, forming diffuse patches that blend into the surrounding substrate.

Dense clusters of small, yellow-green, cup-shaped structures with smooth, rounded edges cover an irregular, similarly colored surface. The cups vary slightly in size and have a matte to subtly glossy texture, closely packed together.

Cluster of small, cup-shaped structures with bright orange discs and pale, raised margins on a rough, yellowish surface. The texture is granular and uneven, with densely grouped, irregularly arranged cups and lobed, undulating edges.

Extremely delicate, dark, hair-like stalks rise from a fine, matted background, each topped with a tiny, glistening droplet-like structure. The fruiting bodies are sparsely distributed and appear very fragile under high magnification.

Leaves display a pale, powdery, whitish to grayish coating forming diffuse, dusty patches across the upper surfaces. Some leaf edges are curled or deformed, with scattered areas of discoloration and necrosis. The powdery growth is patchy but widespread.

Irregular, dark brown to blackish spots and diffuse patches cover the hairy, spiny-edged leaf. The discolorations are flat and scattered, lacking distinct raised structures, blending into the pale leaf surface.

Convex to hemispherical caps with smooth, pale lilac to brownish surfaces, some covered by leaf debris. Gills are closely spaced and light violet. Stipes are short, robust, and pale, with white veil remnants at the base.

Dense cluster of pale greenish to whitish, branched, flattened structures with irregular, contorted forms. Numerous dark brown, rounded to irregular patches are scattered across the surface, giving a mottled, rough, and uneven appearance.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish pustules scattered across the green leaf surface, each surrounded by yellowish halos. The pustules are irregularly distributed, mostly circular to oval, with some minor leaf damage and a slightly hairy texture.
A dense, powdery white to grayish mat covers the leaf surface, forming a fine, continuous layer with a diffuse margin that gradually blends into the green tissue beneath.
Tiny, white, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with conspicuous fringes of fine, hair-like structures around the margins, scattered in small clusters along the surface. The cups appear smooth and delicate.
Small, scattered, darkly pigmented structures embedded in fibrous, rough wood; fungal bodies appear flush with or slightly raised above the surface, blending with the woody texture.

Numerous tiny, rounded, yellowish to pale, slightly translucent fruiting bodies scattered irregularly on a moist, gelatinous surface. The fruiting bodies are minute, embedded or superficial, and lack distinct stalks, contrasting with visible fine hairs and feather structures.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped, smooth ochre to tan caps, some showing a faint pinkish tint. Slender, cylindrical stipes are fibrous and similarly colored. Upturned specimens reveal crowded brownish gills and inrolled cap margins on younger fruiting bodies.

A small, irregular dark brown to blackish patch on the leaf surface, surrounded by a faintly raised, lighter area. The patch is subtle, lacking large fruiting bodies, and sits among fine white leaf hairs.

Powdery, whitish to grayish web-like mats cover the leaf surface, interspersed with denser, slightly brownish granular patches. The fungal growth appears as fine, scattered clusters and delicate, dust-like coatings.

Small mushroom with a slender, smooth, cream-colored stem and a light brown to beige cap. The cap has a slightly wavy margin and a smooth surface. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to off-white, and free to slightly attached.

Leaves display irregular patches of white, powdery coating on their upper surfaces, with some yellowing, browning, and curled edges. The thin, superficial fungal layer is most visible on the green leaf blades.

Cluster of mushrooms with convex, smooth, ochre-brown caps and sturdy, cylindrical stems. Caps show subtle radial streaks and moist sheen. Stems are slightly paler at the base, and the fruiting bodies emerge among dry, brown leaf litter.

Numerous tiny, whitish to translucent, cup-like discs densely scattered across dark, decaying wood. The fruiting bodies are minute, rounded, and slightly granular, with indistinct but slightly raised margins. No visible stalks; arrangement is scattered to gregarious.

Pale brown to grayish caps with a slightly darker center and smooth, moist surface. Caps have gentle umbos and even margins. Thick, widely spaced white gills and slender, smooth white stipes with fibrous bases.

Numerous dark brown to black, circular to irregular spots densely scattered across narrow, elongated green leaves with fine white hairs. The spots are slightly raised and disrupt the smooth leaf surface.
Small, black, flask-shaped dots scattered and partially embedded in weathered wood, with greenish discoloration and moist, textured patches on the stick’s surface.
Irregular brownish to reddish patches with a central whitish spot on a leaf surface, surrounded by dark specks. The texture is rough and uneven, with visible venation and patchy discoloration.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, moist, convex to slightly flattened caps in a purplish-violet hue. Caps show minor blemishes and even margins. Stipes are mostly hidden by leaf litter, with a few pale, slender stems partially visible.

Delicate, translucent cup-shaped fruiting bodies with radiating, feathery margins sit atop slender, dark, hair-like stalks. The base of each cup is slightly yellowish to brownish, and the upper surface shows a fine, filamentous texture. Each stalk supports a single, fragile apothecium.

Narrow, elongated leaves covered with numerous dark brown to black, rounded pustules densely scattered along veins and margins. The pustules are slightly raised, giving a rough, granular texture. Some leaves show browning and withering, with visible fine hairs along the edges.

Numerous tiny, cup-shaped, translucent to whitish fruiting bodies with fine, hair-like fringes are scattered irregularly across the rough wood surface, forming a delicate, low-profile, fuzzy colony. Some cups show slight yellowish or brownish tinges. The apothecia are sessile and lack prominent stalks.

Leaf displays irregular brown and yellow lesions, especially along the edges and between veins. Patchy necrotic spots and crisped, curled margins are visible, with overall discoloration and localized tissue death.

Small, black, globose to subglobose structures clustered and slightly raised above the bark surface, with a rough, textured appearance. The fruiting bodies are embedded in the woody substrate and grouped together, contrasting against the reddish-brown wood.
Dense, rust-brown mass with a granular to powdery texture, tightly clustered and interspersed with fine, filamentous strands radiating outward. The patch stands out against a green background.

Numerous tiny, pale, translucent to whitish cup-shaped structures with thin, delicate margins are scattered and loosely clustered on the surface of a decaying stem. The cups have a smooth, slightly glossy appearance.

Dark, spherical bodies with radiating, hair-like appendages are scattered across a translucent, veined background. The fungal structures appear rough and spiny, grouped irregularly, with dark brown to black coloration contrasting against greenish-yellow hues.

A leaf surface showing a sharp boundary between green and brown tissue, with numerous tiny, dark, dot-like structures scattered across the brown, necrotic area. The surface appears textured and slightly rough.

Pale beige to light brown caps with moist, slightly sticky surfaces and scattered darker spots. Smooth, inrolled margins on young caps, flattening with age. Closely spaced, pale gills and slender, fibrous white stipes, some slightly curved and tapering at the base.

Yellow-green, leafy patches densely covered with small, rounded to cup-shaped orange-brown apothecia. The apothecia have smooth surfaces and slightly raised margins, scattered across a rough, uneven surface tightly attached to a branch.
Green, broad, smooth-edged leaves with minor discoloration or small brownish spots. No visible powdery or fuzzy fungal growth is apparent on the leaf surfaces. Stems bear developing round fruit.
Green leaves display irregular, dark gray to black patchy lesions and spots. The blotches are scattered and sometimes coalesce, distorting the leaf tissue and creating a mottled, uneven appearance.

Rounded, irregular fruiting bodies with a rough, warty, pale tan to pinkish-brown surface, scattered with soil particles. The cut specimen reveals a dense, solid, pale cream to yellowish interior, lacking visible gills or pores. Approximately 2–3 cm in diameter.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised pustules scattered across a green leaf, often surrounded by yellowish halos. The pustules are irregularly distributed, with some areas showing localized tissue damage and minor necrosis.

Numerous tiny, rounded, orange to reddish discs are scattered across a moist, green, granular surface. The discs are smooth, slightly glossy, and emerge directly from the uneven lichenous substrate. Cup-shaped lichen structures and green leaves are visible nearby.

A single, large, rounded orange-brown structure with a granular surface, surrounded by loosely aggregated, amorphous material. The central body is circular with diffuse, mottled coloration and indistinct margins blending into the surrounding matrix.

Small, dark, irregularly shaped patches with a matte texture are scattered across the wood surface. The patches appear cushion-like or crustose, with indistinct, uneven margins. The wood shows pale blue-gray discoloration nearby.

Numerous dark, round to irregular pustules scattered across green leaves and stems, with blackened, necrotic tissue and curling. Fine, web-like mycelial growth is visible along affected areas, causing distortion and damage to the plant.
Irregular circular lesion with a pale, granular center dotted by small dark spots, encircled by a dark brown zone and a prominent reddish margin blending into green leaf tissue.

Round to slightly flattened fruiting bodies with finely granular or warted surfaces, ranging from pale cream to yellowish-brown. Some show darker discoloration, cracks, or splits, and a few have soil remnants on top.
Irregularly globose, clustered fruiting bodies with rough, warty surfaces mottled in brown and tan. Partially covered in soil and organic debris, with white mycelial threads visible at the base.

Numerous small, dark, slightly raised, rounded to irregular bumps scattered across a brown, textured woody surface. The bumps appear as discrete, roughened pustules emerging from the bark, with no visible spore masses or prominent structures.

Leaves display irregular, patchy white discolorations and pale lesions, with some areas appearing necrotic. The affected spots contrast sharply against the otherwise green foliage, creating a mottled appearance.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised pustules scattered across the green, veined, and slightly hairy leaf underside. Some pustules appear powdery and are irregularly distributed along veins and interveinal areas.

Minute, rounded to irregular darkened spots embedded in reddish-brown bark, with some greenish discoloration and slight peeling of the bark surface. The fruiting bodies are scattered and subtle, blending into the rough bark texture.
Round, smooth, brown fruiting body with a moist surface. When cut, reveals a dense, marbled interior that is yellowish to olive-brown, with a thin outer layer and no visible gills or pores.

Numerous small, dark, spherical bodies with radiating, stiff, hair-like appendages are scattered across a green surface, creating a spiky, starburst appearance. The surrounding area has a slightly powdery texture.
Whitish, powdery coating forms diffuse, slightly fuzzy patches on green leaves, with some areas showing concentrated coverage and minor discoloration or necrosis at the edges and tips.

A tiny, delicate fungus with a smooth, pale pinkish-tan, cup-shaped cap atop a slender, slightly curved stipe. The stipe fades from light near the cap to dark at the base, and the margin of the cap appears subtly irregular.
Woody stick densely covered with numerous tiny, dark, dot-like structures scattered across the bark, creating a rough, granular texture. The wood appears dry and partially broken at one end.
A minute, irregularly shaped structure with a granular surface, displaying pale yellowish, brown, and greenish hues. No distinct reproductive features are visible at this magnification.

Brown, conical to convex caps with a pronounced central umbo and fine radial fibrillose texture. Cap margins are faintly striate. Gills are crowded and pale brown. Slender, fibrous stems match the cap color but are slightly lighter.

Extremely small, delicate, dark hair-like stalks rise from the wood, each topped with a tiny, pale, globular or cup-like structure. The fruiting bodies are sparsely scattered, appearing as minute upright filaments with a subtle sheen at the apex.

Dense yellow-green crust with scattered, small, rounded yellow to orange discs. The surface is uneven and granular, with the discs slightly raised and flat to concave, emerging directly from the crust.

Slender, elongated, pale yellow to whitish stalks emerge in irregular, curved, and branched forms from a dark, shriveled base. The surface appears smooth to slightly powdery, with the fungal structures radiating outward in a scattered arrangement.
Tiny, pale to translucent cup-shaped structures with finely fringed edges, clustered and scattered across the surface. The cups are delicate and smooth, appearing almost glassy against the substrate.

Minute, rounded, translucent to pale brownish fruiting bodies clustered in a compact, moist, gelatinous mass. Individual structures are smooth, globose to subglobose, with no visible stipe or cap, and an irregular arrangement.

Dark, irregular patches with a granular, slightly raised texture cover the green leaf surface. Small brownish pustules are scattered within the patches, and the surrounding tissue appears discolored and necrotic. The surface is somewhat glossy with a few visible leaf hairs.

Small, dark, circular to irregular spots with a slightly raised, rough texture are visible on the green leaf surface. The affected areas show minor discoloration and necrosis, with no large fruiting bodies present.

Several tiny, flat, orange-brown disks with smooth edges are scattered across a moist, green, granular surface. The fruiting bodies are minute and disk-like, contrasting with the uneven, textured background and visible lichen thalli.

A thin, whitish, powdery coating forms a diffuse, slightly patchy layer on the leaf surface, giving it a matte, pale appearance. Leaf veins remain visible beneath the subtle fungal growth, with no dense mats or visible fruiting bodies.

Numerous minute, translucent to light brown, globose droplets are scattered across a pale, fibrous surface. The fruiting bodies appear moist, glistening, and semi-embedded, with an uneven, granular texture visible in close-up.

Irregular dark spots and patches with powdery, whitish fungal growth scattered across the green leaf. Small, dark pustules are visible, often surrounded by lighter, discolored tissue. The fungal texture appears powdery to granular, distributed patchily along the leaf veins.
Irregular, rust-brown patches and granular, powdery pustules scattered across a green leaf surface, forming slightly raised, patchy areas with a fine, dusty texture.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded to slightly elongated dots scattered across a brown, necrotic patch on a leaf, with a sharp border between the brown and healthy green tissue. The surface appears rough and uneven, with the dots embedded in the leaf.

Leaves display scattered, small, irregular dark brown to black spots and lesions, some with yellowish halos and advanced necrosis at the margins. Lesions are clearly demarcated from the smooth, glossy green leaf surface.

Minute, rounded, dull grayish to brownish structures with a granular surface, slightly raised and scattered singly or in small groups on a dark, moist background. No stalks or prominent features visible at this magnification.

Clusters of mushrooms with convex, smooth yellowish to ochre caps, some showing faint darker spots. Stipes are pale yellow to cream, with remnants of a web-like veil near the top. Gills are closely spaced and pale, visible in a sectioned specimen.

Irregular dark brown to blackish patches and spots cover the leaf surface, surrounded by yellow and reddish discoloration. The affected areas appear mottled and necrotic, following the veins and interveinal regions of the deeply lobed, spiny leaf.

Rounded, brownish fruiting bodies with a rough, patchy surface, partially covered in soil. One specimen is cut open, displaying a dense, white, marbled interior with a firm texture. The outer layer appears uneven and slightly cracked.
Round to irregular, brown, warty fruiting bodies with a rough exterior. Some are cut open, showing a dense, pale, solid interior. Scattered among grass and moss on the soil surface.

Irregular patches of dark brown to blackish granular spore masses scattered across a pale greenish surface, with fine, web-like hyphal threads radiating outward. The texture appears powdery and embedded within the lighter background.

Small mushroom with a broadly convex, smooth brown cap, darker at the center and lighter at the margin. The margin is irregular and slightly inrolled. Pale, slender stipe is partially visible, with off-white gill edges peeking from beneath the cap.
A dark, elongated lesion with a central split and pale, discolored margin appears on the leaf surface, accompanied by small necrotic spots and holes, indicating localized tissue damage.

Irregularly lobed, subglobose fruiting body with a brown, moist, glutinous surface. Soil particles and organic debris adhere to the exterior, which is mottled with lighter and darker brown patches. No visible stipe or gills.

Irregular, dark brown to reddish-brown necrotic lesions with concentric ring patterns and sharply defined borders contrast against the healthy green leaf tissue. Some lesions appear slightly sunken and scattered across the leaf surface.

Two mushrooms with convex, brownish caps showing paler, fibrous margins and slightly cracked surfaces. The slender, off-white stems are curved, with soil clinging to the base. The caps appear dry and irregular, surrounded by green grass.

A green leaf with a diffuse, white, powdery coating covering much of its upper surface. The powdery layer is most prominent along the central and lateral veins, with patchy areas of denser coverage. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Dense, tangled mat of pale greenish to whitish, branched, flattened structures covered with numerous small, dark brown to nearly black, rough, irregular nodules. The nodules are clustered and warty, contrasting sharply with the lighter, intricate network beneath.

Rounded, light brown fruiting bodies with a smooth to slightly roughened surface. One specimen is cut open, displaying a dense, white, marbled interior without visible gills or pores. Soil and pine needles adhere to the outer surface.

Irregular, patchy yellowish-brown to rusty brown area with a granular, rough texture. Densely packed, tiny rounded brown structures cover the surface, giving it a dotted appearance. Margins are diffuse and blend into the green background.

Clusters of dark, spherical bodies with radiating, rigid, spiny projections form star-like patterns. Each central structure is surrounded by multiple elongated, reddish-brown setae, giving a bristly, spiky appearance against a pale, smooth background.

Small, dark, lens-shaped structures scattered and slightly raised on a woody surface, with rough, darkened tops and faint, lighter fuzzy growth around them. The fruiting bodies are irregularly arranged and partially embedded in the bark.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with pale yellowish to cream tones, some covered in soil and debris. Cap margins are inrolled, surfaces appear velvety. Pale cream, moderately spaced gills are visible on upturned specimens. Short, robust stipes match the cap color.

Numerous tiny, round, orange to reddish discs are scattered across a moist, green, granular surface. The discs are slightly embedded and contrast with the uneven, lichenous background, which features some smooth-edged, grayish lobes and brownish patches.

Two mushrooms with conical to broadly convex brownish caps, some lighter patches, and a slightly wavy margin. Gills are crowded, pale cream to light brown. Stipe is slender, pale, slightly curved, with soil clinging to the base. Cap surface appears fibrous or subtly scaly.

Minute, pale to light brownish rounded discs scattered across a smooth, slightly glistening surface. The fruiting bodies are embedded or slightly raised, with a subtle, even texture and uniform distribution.

Numerous tiny, pale, cup-shaped structures with smooth margins are scattered along the surface of a dead stem. The fruiting bodies are whitish to translucent, very small, and appear sessile without visible stalks.

Small, black, irregularly shaped, and slightly raised bodies embedded in pale, cracked wood. The surfaces are rough, margins indistinct, and the fruiting bodies appear scattered and somewhat clustered, blending into the substrate.

Small, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies with distinct orange-brown discs and pale, whitish, slightly raised margins. The surface appears smooth, and the structures are clustered against a greenish background. Margins are well-defined and contrast with the central disc.

Catkins with small, green, tightly clustered buds, some showing brownish, swollen, or deformed areas. A slight fuzzy coating is visible in places, and the overall texture appears smooth to slightly velvety, with subtle discoloration on affected buds.

Dark, irregular central mass with radiating, hair-like filaments extending outward. Numerous small, spherical bodies cluster around the periphery. The edges appear granular and slightly translucent, with a distinct contrast between the dense center and finer outer structures.
A solitary mushroom with a smooth, moist bluish-gray cap showing subtle radial striations, pale cream closely spaced gills, and a slender bluish-gray stem with a slightly paler base.

Two mushrooms with convex, pale caps covered in fine lilac-tinged granules and a distinct, darker purplish-brown central disc. Cap margins are slightly striate. Slender, smooth white stems support the clustered fruiting bodies above the soil.

Small, clustered cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale yellowish to light brown smooth inner surfaces and slightly darker, finely textured margins. The outer surface is paler and appears minutely hairy or granular.

Several minute, slender, black, upright spike-like structures sparsely emerge from a pale, fibrous woody surface. Scattered greenish patches are visible nearby, with the dark fungal projections contrasting sharply against the light background. No large fruiting bodies are present.

Numerous tiny, black, spherical to slightly elongated structures densely clustered on wood, each adorned with fine, radiating hair-like setae, giving a spiky appearance against the rough, fibrous surface.

Dense, rust-colored, granular patches erupt through a greenish surface, forming irregular, powdery aggregations with reddish-brown coloration and diffuse margins. The texture is granular to powdery, and the distribution is patchy.

Broad, convex to slightly depressed cap with a smooth, pale beige to light tan surface and a few darker spots. The cap margin is entire and slightly wavy. No stipe or gills are visible from this angle.

Cluster of smooth, pale tan to light brown caps with slightly depressed centers and inrolled margins. The caps have a moist, greasy appearance and are closely packed together, showing no visible gills or stems from above.

Clustered mushrooms with smooth, moist, brownish-gray caps that are convex to irregularly lobed and overlapping. The caps have wavy, inrolled margins and a slightly slippery surface, with some pine needles resting on top.

Small, black, rounded to slightly flattened structures scattered and partially embedded in the pale, fibrous plant stem. The fruiting bodies are minute, dark, and subtly protrude from the striated surface, lacking visible stalks or large reproductive features.

A single, small mushroom with a pale lilac to grayish, finely granular cap featuring a striate margin and central depression. The slender, smooth stipe elevates the delicate cap above the soil, contrasting with the nearby cactus.

Numerous small, rounded, white to pale cream structures densely covered in fine, fuzzy hairs, each marked by one or more prominent, dark, nearly black spots. The fruiting bodies are closely packed, with a granular or woolly surface texture.

Rust-colored, oval to irregularly shaped pustules with a granular, powdery texture. The sori are slightly raised, surrounded by a diffuse margin, and densely packed with reddish-brown spores on the leaf surface.

Dense, rust-colored granular patches form irregular clusters, appearing to erupt through the surface. The texture is powdery and spore-laden, with a reddish-brown coloration and slightly raised, rough areas lacking distinct large structures.
Small, rust-colored, slightly raised pustules scattered irregularly on green leaves, often along veins. Some leaves show yellowish discoloration and mild swelling or deformation near the pustules.

Green, pinnately divided leaves with irregular yellowing and browning along the midrib and margins. Some areas appear slightly swollen and discolored, with a rough texture and dense, overlapping foliage. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

White, cottony patches and fuzzy growths are visible on a green catkin, with some buds showing yellow discoloration and slight swelling. The affected areas appear deformed, with the fungal material arranged in small clusters along the catkin.

Slender, whitish stem with a slightly bulbous, lilac-tinged base. Cap is convex, covered in dense lilac-brown granules, with an inrolled, irregular margin. Pale, free gills are visible beneath the cap. Soil clings to the base.

Dense, patchy white cottony mat with numerous minute, rounded dark dots scattered throughout. The surface is uneven and granular, with irregular colonies and scattered yellowish to brownish areas. No large fruiting bodies are visible.

Small, delicate mushrooms with convex to slightly bell-shaped caps, striate margins, and a whitish surface. Gills are free, closely spaced, and cream-colored. Slender, smooth white stems show slight thickening at the base. The overall texture appears fragile.
Kidney-shaped, smooth brown fruiting body with a shiny surface densely speckled with small, white, crystalline or powdery deposits. The margin is well-defined and slightly raised.

Dense, patchy layer of fine, powdery, pale brown to tan growth forms irregular, slightly raised spots and streaks along the leaf veins, creating a mottled, textured surface with minute granular pustules.

Densely packed, coarse, conical to pyramidal brown scales cover the center of the cap, creating a spiky, textured surface with varying dark and lighter brown tones. The background appears dry and fibrous.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded to slightly elongated dots scattered across a brown, necrotic patch of leaf. The affected area appears dry and cracked, with a roughened texture and irregular distribution of blackish structures embedded in the tissue.

A circular, yellowish-brown lesion with a slightly sunken center and a faint lighter margin disrupts the green, hairy leaf surface. The lesion contains a few tiny, pale structures and appears subtly textured compared to the surrounding tissue.

A fine, powdery, pale coating covers the leaf surface, forming a diffuse, slightly raised, patchy layer that follows the contours of the veins. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible, but the texture suggests widespread colonization.

A patch of leaf tissue with a tan to brown, slightly rough and uneven surface, showing subtle irregularities and a faint boundary against surrounding reddish-purple tissue. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Patchy, whitish mycelial mat with a powdery to granular texture, irregularly distributed over a brownish surface. Numerous small, yellowish to orange, rounded structures are scattered and embedded within the mycelium, forming dense clusters in some areas.

Small, dark brown to black, raised pustules scattered across the green leaf surface, each surrounded by a pale, slightly yellowish halo. The pustules are rough and granular, irregularly distributed between prominent leaf veins.

Numerous tiny, pale pinkish to whitish, rounded to slightly flattened discs are scattered across a dense, rough mat of greenish-yellow, branched moss stems. The minute apothecia are embedded or slightly raised, giving a granular texture to the moss surface.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, orange-brown interiors and slightly darker, irregular margins. Fine white mycelial threads are visible at the base, and the cups are closely grouped on a granular surface.
Small, circular to oval lesions with pale, slightly raised margins and ruptured centers exposing tan to brown tissue, scattered across a green, finely haired leaf surface.
Tiny, white to pale cream, globose to slightly club-shaped fruiting bodies clustered densely and scattered, each atop a slender dark stalk, with smooth surfaces amid green moss and decaying stems.

Small, irregular, dark brown to black, slightly raised pustules disrupting the smooth green leaf surface. The pustules have a rough texture and are scattered, contrasting sharply with the leaf’s prominent veins.

A round, compact fruiting body with a densely spiny surface, covered in prominent, conical, light to medium brown scales. The texture appears dry and rough, with no visible gills or stipe from this angle.
Broad, tan-brown cap with a dry surface densely covered in upturned, spiny scales, especially at the center. The margin is slightly irregular, and the overall texture appears rough and scaly.

Small, translucent to light brown disc-shaped bodies with a moist, gelatinous appearance. Surfaces are smooth, some with slightly lobed or irregular margins. A few display tiny white spherical structures on top, scattered loosely across the dark substrate.

Numerous tiny, pale, cup-shaped structures are scattered across a moist, greenish-brown, densely textured surface. The cups are translucent to whitish, sessile, and some have slightly raised margins, blending subtly with the organic debris and mossy background.
A single, ellipsoid spore with pointed ends, a smooth, hyaline wall, and a distinct central vacuole. The periphery appears granular or slightly ornamented, with a clear, well-defined outline.

Small mushroom with a slender, pale, slightly curved stem and a cap viewed from below, showing crowded, creamy white, free gills. The cap margin is striate, slightly upturned, and has a granular or scaly texture.

Dark purple leaf with numerous small, pale, circular to irregular spots scattered across the surface. Some spots coalesce into larger patches, and the tissue around the spots appears slightly sunken and discolored.
Tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a smooth, moist surface and dull brownish to violaceous color. Even margins, sessile, and scattered in small clusters on decaying wood.
Numerous tiny, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised pustules scattered irregularly across a green leaf surface, often concentrated along veins and interveinal areas.

Tiny, dark stalks support disc-shaped, irregular caps densely coated in white, powdery granules. The fruiting bodies are scattered along the substrate, with granular surfaces and a central attachment point visible underneath.
Broad, pale brown caps with a distinct whitish central patch and slightly wavy, irregular margins. Gills are closely spaced, creamy to light brown. Stipe is cylindrical, pale, and smooth.

Irregular, dark brown to black sunken spots with yellowish halos scattered across green and white variegated leaves. The lesions appear dry and necrotic, with some marginal discoloration, clearly visible as localized damage.

Succulent green leaves with pointed, reddish-tipped margins display small, circular, yellowish to reddish raised spots and pustules, some merging into larger discolored patches, especially near the leaf tips.

Numerous tiny, rust-colored, slightly raised pustules are scattered and clustered irregularly across a green, hairy leaf surface. Some pustules are surrounded by faint yellowish halos, breaking through the leaf epidermis. No large fruiting bodies are visible.
Green, fleshy rosettes with smooth, waxy leaves tipped in reddish hues. Some leaves show small, scattered yellowish or brownish spots. Plants are densely clustered among fine, green foliage.

A green, pinnately lobed leaf shows localized, slightly raised, brownish-black lesions with a central necrotic area. The affected region contrasts with the surrounding healthy green tissue, displaying subtle swelling and discoloration.

Numerous tiny, rust-colored, round to irregular pustules scattered across the green leaf surface, some coalescing into larger spots. The pustules are slightly raised and contrast with the leaf’s visible veins and perforations.

A single mushroom with a pale yellowish to light brown, slightly depressed cap, smooth and wavy margin, and closely spaced, cream-colored gills. A broken piece below reveals a white, brittle interior.

Broad, bluish-gray caps with paler, wavy margins and subtle radial streaks. Cap surface appears moist and smooth. Gills are pale cream to light gray and closely spaced. Slender, bluish stipe with a fibrous texture and white base.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, pale yellow to cream inner surface and a distinct, slightly raised brown margin. The outer surface is finely textured. The cup is sessile and directly attached to the substrate.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with pale yellowish to cream discs and slightly darker, fuzzy margins. The apothecia are scattered and sessile on a dark, rough surface, with numerous tiny white spherical structures nearby.

Numerous dark, irregularly shaped, fuzzy patches with diffuse margins are scattered across a lighter background. The texture appears filamentous or hairy, and the coloration is predominantly dark brown to black.
Numerous tiny, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised pustules are scattered across green leaflets, which are covered in fine, whitish hairs. The lesions are minute and irregularly distributed.

Tiny, white, dome-shaped fruiting bodies with a powdery texture sit atop slender, dark stalks, evenly spaced in a neat row along a piece of plant litter. The delicate structures contrast sharply with the linear substrate.

Brown caps with dense, dark, spiny scales concentrated at the center and wavy margins. Stems are covered in brownish tufts. One upturned cap reveals tightly packed, white to cream gills. Young fruiting bodies appear as small, scaly buttons.

Numerous small, rust-brown, circular to slightly oval pustules scattered across a green, hairy leaf surface. The pustules are slightly raised and break through the leaf epidermis, appearing singly and in small clusters.

Numerous tiny, white, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across a brown, veined surface. The discs are smooth, slightly translucent, and have well-defined margins, appearing directly attached without visible stalks.

Two small mushrooms with convex, off-white caps covered in fine granules or scales. The slender, smooth white stems are slightly swollen at the base, with soil attached. Gills are pale and free from the stem, visible beneath the cap edges.
Cylindrical, dark brown to blackish structure densely covered in fine, hair-like setae, giving a velvety, fuzzy texture. Surface appears slightly uneven with minor pitting and irregularities.

Small, circular, rust-colored pustules scattered on the leaf surface, each surrounded by discolored, necrotic tissue. A larger, irregular dark patch is present, with rougher texture and slightly raised margins compared to the healthy green leaf.
Numerous minute, black, bristly structures densely clustered on the wood surface, forming irregular, fuzzy patches with a granular and slightly shiny appearance.

Numerous tiny, rust-colored pustules scattered irregularly across the leaf surface, creating a mottled, slightly roughened appearance with some powdery patches. The pustules are small and do not form large clusters or fruiting bodies.
Robust white stem with some soil debris, closely spaced pale creamy gills, and a smooth, slightly undulating light brown to tan cap margin. Multiple fruiting bodies are clustered together.

Irregular patch of dark brown, rust-colored growth with a granular, powdery texture forming a dense, velvety layer. Coloration is uneven with lighter and darker zones, and the underlying surface is partially visible at the edges.

Clustered, irregularly rounded fruiting bodies with a lobed, cushion-like appearance. Upper surfaces are dark blackish to charcoal, transitioning to brownish tones below, with a velvety to rough, granular texture and some powdery patches.

Dense clusters of irregular, cushion-shaped bodies with dark black to gray surfaces, some covered in pale or rusty-brown speckles. Surfaces appear lumpy, firm, and occasionally cracked, with lighter tan patches on younger or weathered areas.

Delicate, upright fruiting bodies with slender dark stalks topped by globose, pale grayish-white sporangia. The sporangia have a frosted, powdery texture and are scattered across a rough brown surface. A small arthropod is visible among them.
Minute, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with a reddish-brown center and a distinct whitish margin, smooth surface, and scattered arrangement, partially embedded in a granular substrate.

Numerous minute, rounded, dark brown to black pustules scattered irregularly across a pale, slightly fuzzy leaf surface, with a few yellowish spots and visible leaf hairs near the margin. Some pustules are slightly raised and break through the epidermis.

Small, circular, dark brown to black raised pustules scattered across the green leaf surface, some surrounded by faint yellowish halos. The spots are well-defined and distinct against otherwise healthy leaf tissue.
Numerous round to slightly oval, thick-walled brown spores with finely textured surfaces, each separated by clear spaces. The spores display a uniform brown coloration and are not clustered together.

Delicate, upright fruiting bodies with slender, dark stalks supporting globose, powdery grayish-white heads. The sporangia have a granular surface and are scattered across the substrate, some with slightly curved stems.

Small, black, elongated to irregularly shaped fruiting bodies scattered across the surface, appearing slightly shiny and closely attached to the substrate. The structures are distinct, with a somewhat rough, uneven surface and are not densely clustered.
A tiny, dark, nearly spherical fruiting body with a rough, bristly surface and fine hair-like projections, emerging solitarily from the stem. The structure appears irregular and minutely textured.

Slender, fragile mushrooms with pale brown, elongated stems and smooth, conical to convex light brown caps. One cap shows a slightly darker center. Gills are closely spaced and lighter brown, visible on the upturned specimen. Overall delicate and small stature.

Slender, upright, club-shaped fruiting bodies with a deep black, velvety surface. Heads are slightly flattened and irregular, some with subtle grooves or folds. Cylindrical stipes taper smoothly into the heads, forming a small clustered group.
Small, scattered, dark brown to blackish spots dot the fleshy, pointed green leaves with reddish tips and fine marginal hairs. The spots are subtle but distinct against the smooth leaf surface.

Convex to slightly depressed cap with pale brown to ochre tones, closely spaced decurrent gills in light tan to pinkish-buff, robust broken stipe showing a white fibrous interior, and a slightly wavy, irregular cap margin.

Two slender, delicate fruiting bodies with pale lilac to pinkish, slightly fibrous curved stems. Caps are convex to nearly flat, smooth, and pale grayish to light brown with slightly inrolled margins. Pale, closely spaced gills are visible beneath the caps.

Numerous small, rust-colored, irregularly shaped pustules scattered across a green leaf surface. The pustules are slightly raised, rupturing the epidermis and exposing dense, powdery brownish-orange spore masses. Some pustules merge into larger patches, with nearby leaf tissue appearing slightly discolored.

Clustered, rounded fruiting bodies with irregular, lobed shapes. Surfaces are matte black with some lighter grayish to brownish patches, forming a contiguous, tightly packed mass. Texture appears slightly roughened, with no visible reproductive structures.

Green leaf with numerous circular to irregular tan spots, each surrounded by dark purple to brown margins. Some lesions coalesce, and the leaf edges show curling and damage. The surface appears leathery with visible veins.

Tan to brown caps with prominent, dark, spiny or wart-like scales densely covering the surface, especially at the center. The mature cap is convex to flat with a rough texture and slightly irregular margin. Younger, rounder fruiting bodies are also visible.

Small mushroom with a delicate, slightly convex cap showing lilac to brownish tones and a granular, scaly texture, especially at the center. The cap margin is thin and wavy. The slender, pale stipe supports the cap above the soil.

Convex to slightly flattened caps with tan to ochre coloring and a subtly scaly surface. Stipes are robust, white to pale cream, with faint ornamentation and soil remnants at the base. Cap margins are even.

Numerous small, round, dark brown pustules are scattered and slightly raised on the green leaf surface, with some clustering and irregular distribution. The surrounding leaf tissue appears healthy and undamaged.
Small, irregular, swollen yellowish to brownish galls and deformities line the catkin, with some areas showing a fuzzy or velvety texture. The catkin surface appears slightly hairy.
Small mushroom with a convex to flat cap, dark purplish-brown central disc, and paler margin covered in granular, radiating scales. Slender, pale stem. Gills not visible from this angle.

Large, tan-brown cap with a rough, spiky surface densely covered in pointed brownish scales, especially at the center. The margin is slightly wavy. A smaller, globose fruiting body nearby is also densely covered in pointed scales.
Small, black, elongated to irregular fruiting bodies with a slightly shiny surface are scattered in loose clusters and curved lines on a brown, decaying leaf background.

A single mushroom with a hemispherical, convex cap densely covered in coarse, conical brown warts, giving it a spiky appearance. The cap margin is uneven, and the short, robust stem matches the cap's brown coloration. No gills are visible from this angle.

Convex to slightly depressed caps with grayish to bluish tones and subtle radial striations. Cap margins are wavy and irregular. Gills are pale, slightly pinkish, and closely spaced. Slender, cylindrical stipe shows a bluish tint, especially near the top.

A tiny, upright fruiting body with a globose, white to pale gray, powdery surface atop a slender, dark stalk. The surface appears slightly rough or crystalline, and additional blurred fruiting bodies are visible in the background.
Overlapping, fleshy caps with moist, smooth, and shiny surfaces. The caps are irregularly lobed and wavy at the margins, displaying brownish to gray-brown tones with lighter patches near the center.

Minute, rounded to irregular black dots scattered across a pale surface, each surrounded by diffuse reddish to purplish stains. The dark structures contrast sharply with the light background, and no other visible fungal features are present.

Broadly convex cap with a slightly depressed center, warm yellow to orange-brown color, and finely scaly surface. The margin is slightly incurved and even, with darker minute scales concentrated toward the center.

Irregular, dark brown to black lesion with a slightly water-soaked appearance on the green leaf surface. The affected area shows a transition from healthy green to dark discoloration, with visible leaf veins and subtle wilting around the spot.

Numerous tiny, black, elongated to oval spots are scattered in irregular and linear patterns across pale, fibrous, straw-colored stems, giving a distinct speckled appearance. The fruiting bodies are slightly embedded in the surface.

Green leaves display numerous tiny, orange-brown, powdery spots scattered across the surfaces. Some leaves show curling, holes, and necrotic patches, with visible distortion and damage around the rust-colored pustules.

Convex to nearly flat caps with a dry, fibrillose surface, rich yellow to orange-brown with darker scales toward the center. Gills are closely spaced and yellowish. Cylindrical, fibrous stipe is pale yellow to light brown, with no visible ring.

Irregular, spreading, dark olive to blackish, moist-looking mass with a granular, uneven surface and diffuse margin blending into the substrate. A contrasting patch of small, orange, spherical structures appears at one edge.

Dense, powdery mat with a whitish surface, scattered pale orange to salmon-pink patches, and a slightly wrinkled, uneven texture. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible; the growth forms a continuous, velvety layer across the field.
Thin, elongated brown structure with a pointed tip, bearing scattered minute black dots along its surface. The substrate appears dry and slightly rough, with fibrous texture at the base.

Numerous tiny, upright, pin-like dark stalks with rounded heads emerge from a yellow-green, powdery to granular surface coating the wood. The fruiting bodies are scattered and slender, contrasting with the pale, low-growing thallus.

Numerous tiny, dark brown rounded heads sit atop slender stalks, scattered across a granular, yellow-green, powdery surface. The heads contrast sharply with the lighter, crustose background, creating an irregular, clustered appearance.

Pale gray to greenish-gray, cracked and areolate surface with numerous small, black, rounded to angular spots scattered throughout. The texture is rough and granular, forming a patchy, mosaic-like pattern tightly adhering to the rock.

Irregular, polygonal dark lesions form a reticulate patchwork on the leaf surface, separated by lighter tissue. The lesions are slightly raised with a rough, granular texture, displaying brown to grayish tones against the green leaf margin.

Fine, powdery coating with scattered pale spots forms subtle, diffuse patches and minute pustules along the leaf veins and interveinal areas. The fungal growth appears delicate, slightly raised, and whitish to yellowish against the green leaf surface.

A reddish-brown, elongated lesion with a slightly sunken center and diffuse margins appears on a green, linear leaf blade. The affected area shows subtle texture changes and discoloration, with no prominent fruiting bodies visible.

Small, scattered tufts of dark brown to blackish, hair-like filaments form fuzzy clusters on the stem surface. The structures appear fine and hispid, with a distinctly bristly texture under magnification.

A dense, powdery white coating covers the leaf surface, with a fine, granular texture. Scattered dark brown to black spots, some surrounded by pale margins, are embedded within the white mat. Leaf tissue beneath shows discoloration.
