Minute, dark brown to blackish, rounded fruiting bodies scattered across a yellow-green, granular to foliose surface. The fungal structures appear as small, distinct, circular spots interspersed among larger, yellowish-green discs. The overall texture is uneven with irregular arrangement.
A single, globose fruiting body with a bright orange to yellow hue and a rough, cracked surface, standing sessile atop a dark substrate.

Dark, elongated, and slender fruiting body with a curved, tapering projection. The surface is smooth and dark brown to black, with a distinct, narrow neck extending from plant debris. Several air bubbles are visible in the background.

Small, black, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies embedded in reddish-brown bark, some partially exposed in shallow depressions or cracks. The fungal structures appear rough and granular against the bark’s surface.

Bracket-shaped fruiting bodies with rough, zoned brown and tan upper surfaces, velvety to fibrous texture, and wavy, irregular margins. The underside reveals elongated, maze-like pores in a layered, shelf-like arrangement.

Small, black, rounded to slightly elongated fruiting bodies partially embedded in bark, each surrounded by a thin brownish margin. The fruiting bodies are scattered, slightly raised, and have a rough, textured surface.

Dark, irregular patches with a crust-like, rough, and uneven texture cover part of the decaying wood. The fungus appears blackish-brown and blends into the moist, leaf-littered surroundings, lacking distinct fruiting bodies or clear structures.

Green leaf with numerous irregular brown lesions and holes scattered across the surface. Lesions are mostly angular to round, some merging, with slightly darker borders. No visible fruiting bodies or reproductive structures.
Fine, whitish, powdery patches form irregular, slightly raised areas on the upper surface of a green leaf, creating a diffuse coating without visible fruiting bodies.

White, powdery patches form irregular, diffuse coatings on green leaf surfaces, giving them a mottled and slightly granular appearance. The fungal layer obscures the natural leaf color and texture, creating a continuous, superficial film.

Small, delicate mushrooms with thin, elongated stems and pale grayish to whitish, bell-shaped caps. The caps are distinctly pleated with a powdery surface. One upturned specimen reveals dark, radiating gills. The fungi grow in tight clusters.

Numerous tiny, whitish to translucent, disc-shaped fruiting bodies densely clustered along a linear surface. The minute discs have a smooth, glistening appearance and lack visible stalks, creating a delicate, closely packed arrangement.
Dark, branched structure with a rough, hairy surface. A single, round, brownish perithecium with a translucent wall and central ostiole is attached, viewed under high magnification.
Numerous tiny, black, rounded to slightly irregular bumps are scattered across the greenish-brown bark surface, some slightly raised and partially embedded in the substrate.

Small, lens-shaped, darkened structures are slightly raised and embedded in the bark, with rough, granular surfaces clustered irregularly along the wood. The surrounding bark shows subtle discoloration and texture changes.

Pale, crust-like patches tightly adhere to the bark, forming irregular, whitish to pale gray areas with a granular or cracked surface. The coverage is patchy, with some continuous and some fragmented regions. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.

A minute, upright, dark tufted mass with an irregular, bushy outline. Numerous long, hair-like filaments radiate from the central structure, giving it a rough, fibrous texture against the pale, striated surface.

Small, closely packed, upright sporangia with rough, granular surfaces and pale beige to light tan color. Arranged in a linear row, each sporangium is cylindrical to ovoid with a cracked, fragmented appearance. No visible stalks; structures are sessile and under a few millimeters in size.
Clustered, small, rounded yellowish structures with a granular, bumpy surface and patches of whitish or silvery covering, tightly packed along a dark plant stem.
Irregular, patchy encrustations of pale yellow to off-white color form a powdery or granular coating along the surface of a small branch, distributed in a linear pattern.

Numerous tiny, yellowish to pale orange, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered in loose clusters on moist bark. The discs are smooth, slightly translucent, and mostly less than a millimeter wide, appearing embedded or sessile on the surface.

Sharply defined, irregularly angular brown lesion with a lighter, powdery or granular center contrasting against the surrounding green leaf tissue. The lesion’s margins are well defined and the surface appears slightly textured.

Numerous tiny, pale yellow to translucent, gelatinous disc-like and globose fruiting bodies cluster and scatter across the moist, dark wood surface. The fruiting bodies are smooth, sessile, and sometimes slightly lobed or irregular at the margins.
Small, spherical fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly glossy yellowish to ochre surfaces, each elevated on short, slender stalks and grouped closely together on a textured background.
Numerous small, black, irregularly shaped, slightly raised structures densely scattered across a brownish, rough-textured woody surface, giving it a pitted and uneven appearance.
Small, dark, rounded to slightly irregular disc-like fruiting bodies with a smooth, somewhat shiny surface, scattered singly or in small clusters across the moist, decaying wood.

Small, dark, oval to slightly elongated pustules raised above the leaf surface, with a rough, granular texture and a somewhat shiny appearance. The pustules are grouped in small clusters, contrasting against the slightly discolored leaf tissue.
Pear fruit with numerous dark, irregular, velvety spots and patches scattered across yellow-green skin. Lesions vary in size, some coalescing, with surrounding tissue slightly sunken and discolored.

Layered, shelf-like fruiting body with densely packed, elongated, angular pores forming a maze-like pattern. Surface is tan to light brown with a lighter, wavy, and irregular margin. Texture appears tough and woody.

Small, globose to subglobose blackish structures with a rough, granular surface. The fruiting bodies are clustered, somewhat shiny, and display a warty texture against a contrasting yellow-orange background.

A cylindrical ascus filled with several dark, ellipsoid, multicellular ascospores. Some free, septate ascospores are visible nearby, all with a smooth surface and distinct transverse divisions against a plain background.
Tiered, semicircular fruiting bodies with rough, brown, velvety upper surfaces and wavy, irregular margins. The undersides show elongated, maze-like pores, and the texture appears woody and fibrous.

Elongated, branched, septate hyphae with a slightly granular texture and faint greenish-brown coloration. The hyphae are composed of regularly spaced cells, and the branching pattern is clearly visible against a pale background.

Irregular, diffuse white powdery patches cover the upper surfaces of multiple green leaves. The coating appears as fine, powder-like mycelium, forming uneven blotches without distinct fruiting bodies. The underlying leaves remain broad and green, with the white fungal growth distributed across many leaf surfaces.
Small, black, roughly circular to irregular fruiting bodies with a rough, granular texture are partially embedded and slightly raised above cracked, discolored bark, appearing in clustered groups.

Semicircular to fan-shaped brackets in overlapping tiers, with velvety to hairy brown upper surfaces and distinct zonate patterning. Margins are wavy and irregular, and the texture appears tough and woody.
Scattered, dark, fuzzy patches with a dense, bristly texture cover the fibrous plant stems. The fungal growth appears as irregular, hairy clusters composed of fine, dark filaments.

Dark, roughly circular structure embedded in wood, with a rough, uneven surface dotted by multiple small, round black openings. The surface appears matte to slightly shiny, surrounded by fragments of bark.

Numerous tightly clustered, cushion-shaped fruiting bodies with yellowish, wrinkled, papery outer walls. Some are ruptured, revealing dark olive to blackish, granular spore masses. The surface appears powdery in places, and all structures are densely packed, each less than a millimeter across.

Numerous small, black, irregularly shaped, granular patches scattered across a rough, woody surface. The fruiting bodies are low, crust-like, and blend indistinctly into the substrate, lacking prominent stalks or defined margins.

Numerous tiny, black, spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered across a moist, fibrous, decomposed surface with dark brown, reddish, and yellowish hues. The fungal bodies are minute, embedded, and grouped in small, irregular clusters, contrasting with the rough, uneven background.

Patchy, crust-like surface with a granular to areolate texture, predominantly pale green to yellowish-green. The thallus is tightly adherent, uneven, and features small, irregularly shaped patches with scattered, slightly raised granules. No visible reproductive structures.
Minute, dark, star-like or dot-like spots scattered irregularly across the lighter bark surface, forming small, subtle pustules without prominent fruiting bodies.

Small, irregular, slightly raised patches with a rough, cracked surface. Color ranges from muted brown to grayish, blending into the woody background. Discrete pustules show visible fissures and are scattered along the surface.

Creamy white, irregular patches with wavy, undulating margins. Surface appears finely textured and matted, showing subtle zonation and layering. Fruiting bodies are closely attached to the wood, lacking a distinct stem, and have a soft to fibrous look.
Dense patch of green, narrow-leaved plants with some dried, curly stems and seed heads among cut logs and grassy vegetation. No visible fungal fruiting bodies or rust pustules are apparent.

Numerous small, black, circular to irregular, slightly raised fruiting bodies scattered across a pale woody stem, some with a central papilla. Fine whitish mycelial threads are visible among the rough, textured fruiting bodies.

Overlapping, thick, shelf-like clusters with a whitish to pale cream color. Upper surfaces appear velvety or fibrous, with irregular, wavy margins. Some fruiting bodies show a fine, porous underside. Surfaces display scattered debris and slight discoloration.

Numerous small, circular, yellow-orange pustules densely scattered and slightly raised on the green leaf surface, some merging into larger patches. The infected areas appear granular and rough, contrasting with the smoother, unaffected tissue.

Microscopic section showing a gradient from yellowish-brown, fibrous, translucent tissue to a dense, dark, almost black region with irregular, indistinct margins and no visible reproductive structures.

Small, bright orange, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a rough, granular surface and paler, fringed margins. Scattered among green, spiky moss and organic debris, their vivid color stands out against the earthy background.

Tiny, dark olive to brown cup-shaped structures with smooth, slightly glossy surfaces are scattered and sometimes clustered on woody branches. The fruiting bodies have rounded margins and central depressions, blending subtly with the textured wood.
Leaves display a dense, white, powdery coating on their upper surfaces, forming patchy, granular mats that obscure the green color and cause slight discoloration and dullness.

A tiny, solitary fruiting body with a short, pale stalk supporting a dark, cushion-shaped cap. The cap surface appears slightly granular, and the margin is smooth and even, standing out against the woody background.

Small, disc-shaped fruiting body with a pale cinnamon to light brown color, slightly rough matte surface, and irregular, lobed margin. The disc is partially split or cracked and embedded in a moist, green substrate.

Tiny, globose fruiting bodies with a central brown spore mass, each surrounded by a white, irregularly ruffled, papery edge. The peridium is split and peeling away, exposing the inner structure. Fruiting bodies are scattered and measure about 1 mm across.

Thin, creamy white to pale beige crust with a finely pored, granular surface and irregular, wavy margin. The texture appears soft and cottony in places, closely attached to the wood and forming a continuous band.

Tiny, white to pale cream, cup-shaped structures with distinctly fringed, hairy margins are scattered and clustered along a fibrous brown stem. The delicate, translucent fruiting bodies have fine, fuzzy edges and stand out against the textured substrate.
Tiny, hemispherical fruiting body with a smooth, pale brown to white surface. The white membranous outer layer splits and curls outward, exposing a dark, powdery, fibrous spore mass above.
Tightly spaced, pale cream to light beige gills with smooth, even edges and a slightly waxy texture. The gills are attached to the cap and display a regular, parallel arrangement.

Dense, irregularly shaped mass of small, round, brownish spores tightly packed together, displaying a granular texture and uniform size. The spore cluster stands out sharply against the lighter background, with no visible hyphae or other structures.
Tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies in pale orange to salmon hues, each with a distinct white, hairy fringe. Surfaces appear moist and translucent, with some discs adorned by glistening water droplets.

Numerous tiny, dark, nearly spherical bodies with fine, pale, radiating filaments are scattered across a greenish, slightly fuzzy surface. Some yellowish, round structures are also present nearby. The dark bodies measure about 100 micrometers in diameter and are not tightly clustered.

Convex to nearly flat caps with pale beige to light brown coloring and a slightly darker center. Dry, fibrous texture. Gills are closely spaced, pale tan, and attached to slender, off-white stems. Scattered grouping among leaf litter.

Pale whitish to light gray crustose surface with scattered, small, rounded, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised apothecia. The thallus appears granular to roughened, with some yellow-greenish tinges visible in places.

Small mushroom with a conical to bell-shaped, pale grayish cap showing faint radial striations. The slender, straight stipe is pale and slightly fibrous, with a small white mycelial tuft at the base. No veil remnants or ring are visible.

Pale grayish-green, branched, and somewhat flattened thalli with a bumpy, granular surface. The irregular branches are upright and sprawling, interspersed among mossy vegetation, with a distinctly warted texture.

A small, delicate, pale branched structure with a rough, granular surface. The thallus is whitish to pale green, cylindrical, and speckled with darker spots, appearing fragile and minute against the background.

Dense, intricate mat of pale greenish to bluish-gray, contorted and branched lobes with rough, warty, and granular surfaces. Lobes are irregular, some with pointed or spiny tips, and small rounded protuberances. Upright and prostrate forms are tightly clustered together.

Numerous tiny, white to translucent, shallow cup-shaped discs with fine, slightly hairy margins scattered across the surface. Some cups are clustered, and delicate mycelial threads are visible on the substrate.

Small, clustered mushrooms with elongated, grayish ovoid caps showing a powdery surface. Some caps are closed, while others display splitting at the margin. Slender, pale stipes and dark gills are visible, with fruiting bodies densely grouped and overlapping.

Crustose thallus tightly adheres to bark, displaying a granular to areolate texture. Predominantly pale greenish to yellow-green, with some darker or brownish patches. Surface appears cracked and uneven, forming irregular colonies without visible fruiting bodies.

Small fruiting bodies with convex to irregular, velvety orange to apricot caps. One specimen shows closely spaced, pale orange to cream gills that run down a short, robust stipe. Cap margins are smooth and surfaces appear dry.

Dense, powdery white mat covering the green surface, with numerous tiny dark spherical bodies scattered throughout. Yellowish and brownish specks are interspersed within the cottony, irregular fungal layer, which appears patchy and unevenly distributed.

Small, delicate mushrooms with brown, striated, conical to bell-shaped caps and paler margins. White, widely spaced gills are visible on the upturned specimen. Slender, translucent stipes are covered in fine hairs or a frosty coating.

Convex to hemispherical caps with warm brown tones and paler margins. Gills are closely spaced and cinnamon-brown. Cylindrical, pale stipes show brownish fibrils and remnants of a delicate, web-like veil, especially on the younger specimen.
Thin, pale greenish crust with scattered, small, rounded, dark brown to black, slightly raised spots. The surface appears finely textured and patchy, with some granular or powdery areas.

Cluster of small mushrooms with smooth, pale yellow to ochre convex caps, some slightly depressed at the center. Cap margins are even, not striate. Stipes are slender, pale, and cylindrical. The surface appears dry and the mushrooms are scattered on a mossy, lichen-covered substrate.

Green, pinnately compound leaves are coated with a fine, white, powdery layer forming diffuse, irregular patches. The powdery growth gives the leaves a dull, dusty appearance, with some minor discoloration and deformation visible.

Small, dark, rounded to slightly nipple-like fruiting bodies partially embedded in wood, with blackish, slightly shiny surfaces and central openings. Reddish-brown discoloration surrounds the fruiting bodies, which are scattered and blend into the substrate.

Small, dark, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered individually across a smooth, pale stem. The fruiting bodies are blackish-brown, slightly raised, and have a somewhat glossy texture.

A single, circular fruiting body with a pale brownish, finely textured surface and a slightly uneven disc. The margin is distinctly fringed with long, dark, hair-like structures, giving it a ciliate appearance.

Tiny, pale, round caps with a distinctive hairy or bristly texture and fine radiating setae, each perched atop a slender, dark stipe. Fruiting bodies are scattered and delicate, standing at varying heights against a blurred background.

Extensive, crust-like mat tightly covering wood and soil, displaying vibrant orange to rusty-brown hues. Surface appears irregular, woolly to fibrous, with a felt-like texture and diffuse, blending margins.
Tiny, pale cinnamon to tan disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly wrinkled surfaces and even, slightly raised margins, clustered and scattered among green moss on a woody surface.
Scattered, irregular blackish patches with a rough, granular surface are embedded on brown bark. The patches appear slightly raised and contrast with the textured wood beneath.
Overlapping, shelf-like fruiting bodies with a whitish to pale cream color and light brown areas near the base. The surface is rough, uneven, and zonate, with rounded, slightly lobed margins.

Powdery, whitish patches cover the leaf, dotted with numerous tiny, dark, spherical to oval fruiting bodies and scattered yellowish granular spots. The fruiting bodies are irregularly distributed, and the leaf shows areas of discoloration.

Small, olive-brown fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly translucent surfaces. Some appear as open cups with distinct margins, while others are more globose or bell-shaped, emerging scattered from moist, textured wood.

Tiny, pale cream to whitish caps with faintly pleated surfaces sit atop long, slender, dark brown to blackish stems. Some caps reveal white, widely spaced gills. The delicate mushrooms are scattered sparsely across decaying leaves.

Several dark, nearly spherical, smooth and glossy sporangia are borne on delicate, transparent, hair-like stalks. The sporangia are deep blackish in color and distinctly separated, with thin, elongated, hyaline stalks visible under magnification.

Small, mostly spherical fruiting bodies with a dark brown center surrounded by a white, irregularly lobed or frilled outer layer. The white margin appears brittle and fragmented, exposing the darker interior. Structures are scattered and only a few millimeters wide.

Thin, continuous crust with greenish to yellow-green coloration and a granular, uneven surface. Numerous rounded, pale to yellowish discs with slightly raised margins are scattered centrally, contrasting with the thallus. Edges are irregular and diffuse.

Irregular, crust-like patches with a rusty orange-brown color and a fibrous, granular texture. The surface is lumpy and uneven, closely attached to woody fragments, with some darker, almost blackened areas.

Numerous tiny, black, spherical to oval bodies densely scattered across a fibrous, moist surface, giving it a peppered appearance. The black structures are closely grouped and appear on very short, barely visible stalks.
Small, bright orange cup-shaped fruiting bodies with distinctly fringed, whitish margins and finely granular surfaces, scattered among dense green and brown moss tufts.

Extensive, crust-like patch tightly adhering to wood, with a yellowish-brown, fibrous to felted surface and irregular, diffuse margins blending into the substrate. The texture appears rough and uneven, lacking any distinct cap or stem.

Numerous tiny, dark, dot-like structures scattered across a discolored, brown and purplish leaf surface. The spots are slightly raised and irregularly distributed, with the leaf showing a leathery texture and patchy coloration.

Numerous tiny, whitish to pale cream, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, rounded margins are scattered irregularly across the wood surface. The delicate, somewhat translucent cups are sessile and lack visible stalks.

Dense, felt-like surface with a rusty brown coloration, appearing fibrous and matted. The texture is uneven and granular, with small, irregular patches and no distinct fruiting bodies visible under high magnification.

A small mushroom with a conical to bell-shaped cap, pale beige to slightly pinkish in color, and a finely textured surface. The slender, smooth white stem lacks a ring or volva. Gills are not visible from this angle.

Small, black, circular to irregular fruiting bodies scattered and slightly sunken in pale wood, each with a rough surface and a central opening. Margins are distinct and slightly raised, giving a textured, grouped appearance.
Small, dark, circular to slightly elongated raised spots scattered across a smooth, pale woody surface. Some spots have a central dot or opening, and the wood shows faint longitudinal lines.
Numerous tiny, pale, cup-shaped fruiting bodies less than a millimeter wide, some with fine, hair-like margins, are scattered irregularly across the fibrous, weathered wood surface.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly attached to the surface, pale off-white to light beige, with a finely granular, powdery texture. Subtle cracks and irregular, indistinct margins blend into the background. No visible fruiting bodies or prominent structures.

Clustered, small mushrooms with elongated, grayish to brownish caps, some intact and others splitting or dissolving. Caps have a powdery or fibrous texture. Slender, pale stems with remnants of veil tissue are visible, giving a delicate, fragile appearance.

Dense clusters of small, dark, shiny spherical bodies are interwoven with fine, translucent threads. The mycelium appears pale and wispy, contrasting with the smooth, closely grouped fruiting structures.

Clustered mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed brown caps, darker central discs, and striate, translucent margins. Gills are pale cream to light tan and attached to slender, smooth, pale to grayish stipes. Radial fibrillose texture is visible on the cap surface.

Two mushrooms with convex, smooth, orange-brown caps and closely spaced pale brown gills. Cylindrical, fibrous stems show soil and mycelium at the base. Cap margins are even, and both fruiting bodies are nestled among leaf litter.

A delicate mushroom with a slender, whitish stem and a conical to bell-shaped, pale gray cap covered in fine, powdery texture. The cap margin is slightly incurved, and dark gills are visible beneath. Soil clings to the base.

Thin, crust-like layer tightly appressed to the wood, pale grayish-green with densely packed small circular fruiting bodies. Each fruiting body has a distinct pale margin and darker center, creating a ringed or star-like appearance. Texture appears powdery to granular.

Creamy white, shelf-like fruiting body with a thick, fleshy texture and wavy, irregular margin. Surface appears smooth to slightly fibrous, with brownish discoloration near the base and edges. Laterally attached to wood.

Close-up of closely spaced, radially arranged gills with a smooth, slightly velvety texture. The gills are attached to a central, cylindrical, smooth, pale stipe. Coloration transitions from light beige to brown, with even, unnotched gill edges.

Small, dark brown to black, cup-like fruiting bodies tightly clustered along a woody stem. The surface appears rough and somewhat glossy, with a moist texture. No gills or pores are visible, and the fruiting bodies are diminutive in size.

Tiny, pale convex caps perched atop long, thin, dark wiry stems, scattered singly and upright above moist, decaying leaves. The fruiting bodies are delicate and widely spaced, with smooth caps and slender stalks emerging from the leaf litter.

Dense, rusty orange to brown crust-like mat with a felted, woolly texture. Surface is uneven, granular, and patchy, with lighter whitish areas at the margins and some fibrous or tufted zones closely adhering to the wood.

Dense, felt-like patch with a fibrous, matted texture and yellowish-brown coloration. The surface appears irregular and fuzzy, with fine, hair-like structures extending outward. No distinct cap or stem is visible, and the fungus spreads flatly over the substrate.

Tiny, cup-shaped, translucent yellowish fruiting bodies with a moist, glossy surface. Each cup is adorned with prominent, radiating, hair-like bristles along the upper margin, giving a spiky appearance. The structures are scattered and partially embedded.

Clusters of dark, nearly spherical bodies with glossy surfaces, each encircled by numerous long, thin, translucent filamentous appendages. The structures are closely grouped on a fine, pale green, slightly fuzzy background.

Clustered fruiting bodies with oval to cylindrical caps covered in a whitish, powdery coating. Mature caps elongate, showing splitting and inky black margins. Stipes are white and fibrous, with an overall pale to grayish appearance.

Small, clustered, translucent to whitish globose structures with a smooth, moist, gelatinous appearance. The fruiting bodies are tightly grouped, forming a patch with irregular, somewhat lobed outlines, as seen in the magnified inset.

Tiny, disc-shaped fruiting bodies with pale orange to salmon coloration and distinctly hairy, fringed margins. Surfaces appear moist and slightly translucent, with some droplets of water present. The delicate structures are closely grouped and minute in size.
A thin, powdery white coating covers the leaf surface, with scattered tiny dark specks visible across the green leaf, giving it a dusty, mildewed appearance.

A tiny, dark brown to blackish, cup-shaped fruiting body with a slightly roughened surface and a central, shallow disc-like depression. The margin is even, and the structure sits directly on textured, light brown bark.

Small, black, rounded fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, smooth, desiccated needle. The surface shows occasional white patches, with the black structures slightly raised and embedded in the tissue.

Long, slender, transparent hair-like stalks each bear a single, smooth, round, dark sporangium at the tip. The sporangia are globose and nearly black, with sparse, separate arrangement across a pale background.
Tiny, scattered, blackish, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a smooth, somewhat shiny surface, appearing superficially on a pale stem and distributed irregularly along its length.

Dense mat of fine, whitish threads covering a greenish surface, scattered with numerous tiny, spherical to ovoid dark brown, reddish-brown, and yellow bodies, each bearing long, thin, hair-like appendages radiating outward.

Tiny, rounded fruiting bodies with a white, star-like, radiating peridium that peels back to reveal a central, powdery dark brown spore mass. The peridium is papery and crisp, with irregular margins. Each structure is about 1 mm wide.
Tiny, scattered cup-like or globose structures with whitish or silvery outer layers and dark centers, appearing powdery and delicate, are loosely grouped across the decaying wood surface.

Clustered, elongated caps with a whitish, powdery or shaggy surface. Some caps are beginning to dissolve, exposing black, crowded gills. Stipes are white, fibrous, and slender, emerging from dark soil among fallen leaves.

Pale beige cap with smooth margin, showing closely spaced, cream to light tan gills beneath. Cylindrical, fibrous stipe with brownish markings. Gills are well-developed, with a small area of damage visible. Moderate size, solitary fruiting body.

Small, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with a dark, nearly black exterior and a striking yellowish inner area. The surface appears granular and rough, with irregular margins. The cups are scattered and emerge distinctly from the substrate.

Two minute fungi with thin, wiry, reddish-brown stems and tiny, white, umbrella-shaped caps. The caps are finely hairy at the edges, giving a delicate, fringed appearance. Each fruiting body stands singly on decaying leaf surfaces.

Small, scattered, dark, irregularly shaped patches embedded in the bark surface, appearing slightly raised with rough, crustose texture. The fruiting bodies have indistinct, irregular margins blending into the mottled greenish-brown bark.
Tiny, delicate mushrooms with thin, dark, wiry stems and pale, pleated caps. Some caps are convex, others show widely spaced white gills from below. Fruiting bodies are scattered and slender.

Brown, textured surface densely dotted with numerous tiny, black, rounded to slightly irregular spots embedded in the tissue. Fine venation and scattered fibrous strands are visible across the surface.

Leaves display a dense, white, powdery coating forming irregular patches on the upper surfaces, giving them a pale, silvery appearance. Some areas show heavier coverage, while others remain partially green beneath the powdery layer.

A thin, irregular fragment of plant material with a single, small, pale, conical fruiting body emerging from its surface. The fruiting body is smooth, slightly translucent, and pointed at the apex. The substrate appears fibrous and rough.

Dark, roughly triangular to irregular, slightly raised fruiting bodies break through the brown bark, forming fissures and slits. The fungal structures are scattered and appear as darker, roughened patches against the dry woody surface.

Small to medium mushrooms with pale yellow to cream, smooth, slightly convex to flattened caps. Gills are closely spaced, decurrent, and pale cream, extending down short, robust, similarly pale stipes. Some caps show subtle zonation and soil debris adheres to the base.
Small, white, cottony tufts of mycelium emerge from the leg joints and body segments of a spider, forming distinct pads that contrast sharply with the spider’s slender, brown limbs.

Dense clusters of minute, black, rounded fruiting bodies tightly packed on decaying wood, forming irregular granular patches that contrast sharply with the lighter substrate. No stalks or large structures are visible.
Small, dark, spherical fruiting bodies with a matte, velvety surface, each elevated on a short, pale stalk. The sporangia are closely grouped, emerging from a white, cottony base atop green leaves.

A spider with a dense, white, fuzzy or powdery mass covering its body, especially on the dorsal side. The spider’s legs are splayed and lifeless, with the fungal growth appearing cottony or granular against the dark background.

Cluster of pale, off-white to light gray mushrooms with wavy, irregular caps and thin, undulate margins. Gills are white, crowded, and run down the slender, slightly curved stipes. Caps have a dry, fibrous texture.

Small, dark, scattered spots and patches are visible on the leaf surfaces, blending in and causing slight discoloration and minor deformation. The fungal structures are minute, flat, and not highly raised, distributed across several serrated leaves.

Whitish, powdery growth covers the spider’s body and legs, forming patchy, cottony tufts, especially around the joints and abdomen. The spider’s legs are splayed, with visible fungal encrustation creating a distinct, textured appearance.

Numerous tiny, white, cup-shaped structures with a delicate, crystalline appearance are scattered across the dark, decaying wood surface. The fruiting bodies are minute and grouped irregularly, standing out against the moist, partially decomposed bark.
A faint, powdery white coating forms a thin, patchy, and slightly granular layer on the green leaf surface, following the veins and contours without distinct reproductive structures visible.
Whitish, powdery coating forms irregular, diffuse patches on the upper surfaces of green, serrated leaves, giving them a dusty appearance and partially obscuring their natural color and venation.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, granular sporangia scattered and clustered along leaf veins, each supported by delicate whitish threads. The sporangia form loose, irregular aggregations, creating a fine, powdery appearance contrasting sharply with the green leaf surface.

Crustose, granular thallus forming a patchy layer of small greenish to whitish granules and splotches, tightly adhering to rough, cracked bark. Texture is rough and irregular, with some powdery areas and tiny dark rounded spots scattered throughout. Overall coloration blends pale green, white, and brown.

Small mushrooms with convex to slightly depressed, dark grayish-brown caps featuring striate, wavy margins. Gills are pale cream to gray and closely spaced. Slender, grayish stems have whitish bases with soil or mycelial remnants. Caps appear smooth.

Numerous small, rounded to oval, dark brown to blackish fruiting bodies with a slightly raised, granular or roughened texture, some showing a lighter, powdery surface, scattered across a pale greenish-yellow background.
Dense, white, powdery mass envelops the spider’s abdomen, with a granular to fluffy texture. Smaller white tufts are visible on the legs, contrasting with the spider’s slender, brown limbs.
Small, dark, circular to oval disc-like structures with slightly raised margins and darker centers, embedded in a pale, granular surface covered with fine, hair-like filaments.

A spider with its body enveloped in dense, white, powdery fungal growth, especially on the abdomen and thorax. The fungal mass appears granular and cottony, with mycelium emerging from the host. The spider’s legs are splayed and desiccated.

Spider legs and body densely covered in thick, white, powdery to cottony mycelium, creating a fuzzy, filamentous texture that obscures natural features. The fungal growth appears evenly distributed, with no visible fruiting bodies.

Whitish, powdery and cottony growth covers the spider’s body and legs, forming dense, fluffy clusters and granular patches, especially at joints and segments, giving a frosted, scattered appearance along the appendages.

A single, smooth, pale oval sporocarp with numerous slender, translucent stalks radiating outward, each ending in a small, fuzzy or granular cluster. The overall appearance is delicate, with a soft yellowish-beige coloration.
A spider's body is enveloped in dense, white, cottony mycelium with fluffy, filamentous outgrowths radiating from its legs and body, creating a starburst-like appearance.

The texture shifts from a compact, darker upper region to a looser, paler interior. Margins are uneven, with coloration ranging from pale to brownish hues.

Small, black, shield-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly shiny surfaces and well-defined margins, scattered and slightly raised above the brown woody surface. Some show fine longitudinal ridges or a central slit.

Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly elongated fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on the dry, brown, ridged surface of woody twigs. The fruiting bodies appear as dark dots embedded in the bark, with no visible clusters or surrounding discoloration.
Elongated pale stems with scattered, dark, linear to irregular patches and spots. The darkened areas are slightly raised or cracked, contrasting with the otherwise smooth surface of the stems.

Numerous minute, pale greenish-yellow, pin-like structures with tiny rounded heads atop slender upright stalks are scattered sparsely and evenly across the wood surface. The delicate fruiting bodies appear smooth and very small, emerging directly from the substrate.

Granular, crust-like surface tightly attached, displaying pale greenish-gray to brown mottling. Numerous tiny, rounded, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised apothecia are scattered irregularly. The thallus is cracked, uneven, and interspersed with yellowish-green patches, giving a patchy, textured appearance.
Dense, cushion-like mats of intricately branched, pale green to whitish, bushy structures with finely divided, irregular margins. The surface appears compact and globular, partially covered by snow.

A minute, dark, irregularly globose fruiting body embedded in a pale, fibrous surface, exuding a single tiny whitish droplet from its tip. The texture appears rough and granular, and the structure is solitary.

Small, rounded fruiting bodies embedded in bark, each with a central opening and radiating star-like fissures. The surface is smooth and slightly sunken, with a subtle color contrast against the woody background.

Elongated, transparent, tubular structures with smooth surfaces, some containing developing internal bodies. The structures are hyaline and colorless, sharply outlined against an indistinct background.

Numerous small, black, rounded to slightly flattened dots are scattered irregularly across a smooth, brown, longitudinally ridged twig. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and embedded in the bark, blending subtly with the wood’s surface.

A pale, swollen, and distorted patch appears on a green leaf, with a whitish, thickened texture that contrasts sharply against the surrounding healthy foliage. No prominent fruiting bodies are visible.
A dark, circular, slightly raised lesion with a cracked surface and irregular margin on green bark. The center is darker, and some greenish material is present on and around the lesion.
Small mushrooms with convex to nearly flat, pale yellowish-tan smooth caps. Gills are closely spaced, pale cream to light brown, and the slender white stems have soil remnants at the base.
Dark, irregular, slightly raised lesions with cracked, rough surfaces and lighter patches are scattered along the greenish branch, disrupting the smooth bark texture.

Small fruiting bodies with convex to slightly umbonate, pale pinkish-salmon caps about 1 cm wide, finely striate margins, widely spaced pale gills, and slender cylindrical stipes bearing mossy or soil remnants at the base.

Numerous tiny, dark, nearly spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered across a pale, striated surface. The fruiting bodies are deep brown to almost black, rough or granular, and densely clustered in some areas, more sparse in others.
A minute, solitary, blackish, globose fruiting body with a smooth surface, perched on wood. Fine, hair-like structures are visible at its base amid woody debris.

Small, dark brown to nearly black, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies scattered and partially embedded in pale, fibrous wood. The fruiting bodies are subtle and lack prominent external structures.

Small, delicate mushroom with a slender, light brown stem and a smooth, conical to bell-shaped cap. The underside reveals closely spaced, pale brown gills radiating from the stem. No ring or veil remnants are visible.

Irregular, dark crust-like patches embedded in rough wood, with slightly raised, cracked margins and scattered minute reddish to blackish dots. The fungal growth contrasts with greenish areas on the surface.

Small, black, oval to irregularly shaped fruiting bodies clustered on a woody surface, some with subtle red tinges. The surface is rough and granular, with greenish patches of moss or lichen. The fruiting bodies are partially embedded and scattered in loose groups.

A cluster of upright, slender, stalk-like structures with slightly swollen, roughened tips. The stalks are pale greenish to brownish, with a granular or powdery surface, irregularly spaced, and interspersed among earthy, lichenous material.
Numerous spherical to subspherical, thick-walled bodies with a rough, net-like surface pattern, densely clustered and colored deep orange to brown, set against a translucent background.

Numerous tiny, bright red, globose to subglobose, translucent fruiting bodies cluster on a dark, rough, cushion-like surface. The fruiting bodies appear moist, smooth, and lack visible stalks, standing out sharply against the dark background.

Small, dark, fuzzy tufts with radiating, hair-like projections are scattered irregularly along the smooth surface of a plant stem. Each tuft appears blackish-brown and forms a distinct, spiky cluster.

A cluster of minute, pale, granular or powdery structures, whitish to cream in color, forming irregular, dense patches with a crustose, granular texture. The background is blurred, highlighting the compact aggregation of the fungus.
Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised pustules scattered across the surface of a green leaf, with some minor holes and irregular leaf edges.

Broad, reddish-brown caps with a smooth, moist surface and slightly wavy margins. Gills are crowded and pale brownish. Stipes are robust, pale with faint brownish or lilac tinges, and display subtle longitudinal fibrils.

Small, irregularly crescent-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, moist, glossy surface. Color transitions from yellowish to brownish, with a darker, well-defined margin. Texture appears gelatinous and soft, with light reflecting off the wet surface.

Numerous tiny, nearly black spherical or irregular specks are scattered and clustered across the brown wood surface, interspersed with small, pale, irregular fragments. No large fruiting bodies are visible; the dark colonies appear minute and densely grouped in places.

A cluster of withered, brownish floral tissues with curled, desiccated petals and sepals. Dark, granular patches are visible among the dry, papery textures, giving an irregular, contorted appearance with muted coloration.
A small, solitary mushroom with a smooth, light brown, conical to bell-shaped cap. The cap margin is even and not striate. The slender, pale stem is mostly hidden by surrounding green grass.

Tiny, yellow-orange, cushion-shaped structures with a central dark spot are scattered across a dark, mottled surface. The fruiting bodies are slightly raised and have a granular texture, standing out against the decomposing substrate.
Numerous tiny, dark, slightly raised dot-like fruiting bodies are scattered irregularly across the light brown to grayish bark of a woody stick, creating a speckled appearance.
Small, rounded, blackish fruiting bodies embedded in a patch of lighter brown tissue on wood, appearing as distinct, slightly raised, smooth dark spots clustered within a defined area.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded to slightly irregular dots are scattered across a pale, fibrous wood surface. The fruiting bodies are minute, slightly raised, and vary in density, with some closely grouped and others more isolated.

Tiny, rounded to irregular reddish-brown fruiting bodies with a finely textured, granular surface, scattered and sometimes clustered directly on fibrous plant debris. The fruiting bodies are sessile and lack visible stalks or distinct margins.
A rough, uneven surface with fine cracks and mottled tan to brown coloration, scattered with multiple small, dark, rounded spots of varying size irregularly distributed across the field.
Tiny, dark, nearly spherical fruiting bodies scattered across fibrous wood, each with a smooth to slightly roughened surface and a subtle glossy sheen.

Small, circular, dark brown to reddish-brown disc with a slightly raised, smooth surface and well-defined margin. Several smaller, similarly colored discs are scattered nearby on the yellowish-brown substrate.

Numerous small, dark, nearly spherical to slightly irregular spots scattered across a pale, fibrous surface. The blackish to deep brown structures are discrete, slightly raised, and give a granular texture, with some clustering visible.

Minute, rounded, slightly raised brownish structures scattered irregularly across the woody surface, with a smooth texture and subtle size variation. Fruiting bodies are spaced apart or in loose clusters, lacking prominent margins or visible openings.

Delicate mushrooms with slender, pale stems and smooth, conical to bell-shaped tan caps showing fine striations at the margin. Gills are closely spaced, pale beige, and visible beneath the caps. Fruiting bodies vary from conical to expanded forms.

Numerous small, circular, dark reddish-brown to purplish spots with defined margins and occasional central depressions are scattered across the green leaf surface. Some spots are slightly raised and coalesce into larger patches.
Several brownish, spherical to subspherical structures with rough, reticulated surfaces and distinct polygonal, net-like ridges, grouped closely together against a pale background.

Dense, blackish to dark brown powdery masses clustered inside a withered, curled flower head. The fungal growth has a granular texture, replacing the normal floral structures and contrasting with the dry, desiccated petals and sepals.

Irregular, dark brown to black spot with sharply defined edges on a green leaf. The surrounding tissue is yellowed and water-soaked, with brown streaks and scattered tiny black specks. Fine marginal hairs and smooth veins are visible.
Tiny, light brown to tan disc-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth surfaces and even margins, each atop a slender, pale to whitish stem, scattered along a piece of dead wood.

Tiny, scattered, dark brown to black circular structures with slightly raised profiles and central depressions are embedded in the yellowish wood surface. The fruiting bodies are minute and subtly disrupt the otherwise smooth texture of the substrate.

Numerous small, black, slightly raised, rough-textured fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across dark, moist bark with patches of green moss and peeling areas. The fruiting bodies are embedded and granular in appearance.

Pale greenish to whitish, tightly adherent crust with a cracked, areolate surface. The texture appears granular and uneven, with fine fissures and subtle color variation. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Medium-sized mushrooms with smooth, moist brown convex caps, closely spaced pale to lilac gills, and robust white to pale lilac stipes, some showing faint violet tints. Cap margins are smooth, and soil clings to the stipe bases.

Small, rounded, dark brown to blackish fruiting bodies scattered and slightly raised on pale wood, with a smooth, somewhat glossy surface. The fruiting bodies are loosely grouped and partially embedded, contrasting with greenish patches nearby.

Small mushrooms with convex to conical caps, dark brown centers fading to tan margins, and pronounced radial striations. Gills are pale brown, closely spaced, and slightly decurrent. Slender, smooth, pale stipes with a translucent quality.

Clustered mushrooms with convex, moist brown caps showing darker streaks and wavy margins. Gills are close and brownish, stipes are pale with brown streaks and soil remnants at the base. Cut specimen reveals a white to pale interior. Cap surface appears smooth to slightly fibrillose.

Elongated green leaf with irregular, pale tan to brown lesions featuring diffuse, indistinct margins. No visible fruiting bodies. Lesions contrast against the healthy green tissue, creating patchy discoloration along the leaf surface.

A green, ribbed flower bud with tightly clustered segments stands beside delicate, white, feathery seed structures. The bud surface is smooth and unbroken, with no visible discoloration or fungal growth.

Numerous tiny, dark brown to blackish, dome-shaped fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across pale wood, each slightly flattened and embedded, some with a small central opening. The surface appears rough and subtly textured.
Tiny, dark brown to nearly black, smooth, spherical fruiting bodies scattered across fibrous, decaying wood. The sporocarps are minute, glossy, and grouped in small, dispersed clusters.

Numerous small, spherical, brownish-gold structures with a granular texture are scattered and closely grouped. Some appear translucent and refractive, set against a background of amorphous organic material under microscopic view.

Numerous thin, intertwined dead branches with rough, mottled surfaces rest atop a dense layer of dry, thatched wood. No distinct fruiting bodies or reproductive structures are visible; surfaces appear irregular and possibly dusted with fine growth.
Numerous tiny, pale cream to off-white, disc-shaped structures with smooth, slightly granular surfaces and rounded edges, clustered irregularly on a woody surface.

Several flower heads are darkened, shriveled, and deformed, with irregular black, powdery masses replacing the normal floral parts. The black fungal growth appears granular and concentrated within the flower heads on upright stems.
A single, elongated, translucent spore with a smooth surface and multiple internal cross-walls, slightly curved and set against a pale, featureless background.
Numerous tiny, rounded, dark brown to blackish dots scattered irregularly across the fibrous wood surface, each slightly raised and embedded, with smooth surfaces and no visible stalks.

Numerous small, rounded to irregular, yellowish-ochre disc-like structures scattered and slightly raised above the pale, weathered wood surface. The fruiting bodies are smooth, embedded or just above the substrate, and show some clustering with variable sizes.
Numerous tiny, dark, rounded dots scattered irregularly across a pale, slightly yellowish wood surface. The dots appear embedded or slightly raised, with no visible mycelial mat or other structures.

Numerous small, dark, ellipsoid to slightly curved spores are scattered densely across the field, with some forming clusters. Amorphous, darker fragments are interspersed among the spores, all viewed under high magnification.
A tiny, delicate, club-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, white, slightly curved upper portion and a thin, dark stem attached to a brown, veined leaf surface.

Small, irregularly shaped structure with a light brown, granular surface. Several dark, nearly black rounded spots are clustered centrally. Margins are uneven and somewhat angular, with no visible substrate.

Close-up of tightly packed, ochre to light brown gills radiating from a slender, cylindrical stipe. The gills are smooth and even with a slightly waxy texture. The stipe shows minor surface damage and a delicate, textured appearance.

Small, dark brown to black, hemispherical fruiting bodies with smooth, slightly shiny surfaces, scattered and partially embedded in the woody substrate. The fruiting bodies are uniform in size and irregularly spaced.
Fine, dark, hair-like filaments emerge in tufts from a dried plant stem, forming delicate, spidery clusters with small darkened points where the filaments originate.

Numerous minute, dark brown to black, nearly spherical fruiting bodies are scattered across a rough, fibrous, and fragmented brown surface. The sporangia are smooth to slightly textured and very small, each less than 1 mm in diameter.

A small, dark, roughly circular to pear-shaped structure with a distinct central opening, partially exposed by torn bark. The surface appears rough, and the surrounding wood shows reddish and yellowish discolorations.

Several flower heads are darkened, shriveled, and deformed, with blackened, papery, and collapsed textures. Some display irregular, dry surfaces and dark powdery masses, contrasting with healthy green stems and fluffy white seed heads nearby.
Numerous small, dark, roughly spherical to slightly irregular fruiting bodies with a rough, granular texture are clustered and scattered on the light brown, fibrous wood surface.

Cluster of mushrooms with smooth, moist, convex to flat caps in violet to brownish hues. Gills are closely spaced and pale violet. Stipes are robust, cylindrical, whitish with violet tinges, and soil remnants at the base. Some caps show a slight umbo.
A woody stick densely covered with numerous small, black, rounded to slightly irregular fruiting bodies, each matte and slightly raised or embedded in the surface.

Irregular, bright yellow-green patches with a powdery or granular texture spread across the bark of logs. The growths are flat, amorphous, and closely appressed, with diffuse, uneven margins that stand out against the dark, rough bark.
Sparse, upright, dark hair-like structures emerge from a brown, uneven, moist-looking surface. The bristles are thin and scattered, standing out against the glossy texture of the substrate.

Irregular, flattened yellowish to ochre patches with rough, cracked surfaces and uneven, lobed margins. Some areas show darker, possibly mature or damaged sections. Growth is closely appressed to the substrate and scattered.

Tiny, pale whitish cup-shaped structures with slightly translucent, minutely fringed margins, scattered across a brown, textured surface. The fruiting bodies are delicate, sessile, and appear finely granular at the edges.

Slender, orange to yellowish, thread-like fruiting bodies emerge upright from moist, decaying leaves and needle litter. The filaments are smooth, thin, and scattered, lacking caps or gills, and contrast against the dark, decomposing substrate.

White, powdery patches cover the upper surfaces of green leaves, giving them a silvery, dusty look. The fungal coating appears in irregular shapes and varies in density across the foliage, contrasting with the vibrant pinkish-red flower clusters.

Pale grayish-green, patchy mat with irregular, granular surface and small, lobed margins. The thallus appears slightly powdery, forming scattered, overlapping patches closely adhering to the rough bark.

Dark brown to nearly black, cup-shaped fruiting bodies with smooth to slightly wrinkled inner surfaces and irregular, undulating margins. The outer edges are paler and somewhat roughened. The cups are sessile and grouped closely together.
Tiny, pale whitish cup-shaped structures with finely fringed margins, appearing slightly translucent. The fruiting bodies are minute, smooth, and scattered, each directly attached to the surface.
Thin, patchy cream to off-white crusts spread irregularly across the wood surface, forming a smooth, somewhat waxy layer with diffuse, indistinct margins blending into the substrate.
A small, cushion-shaped fruiting body with a light brown to ochre color and a rough, granular surface, attached to a mossy, decaying branch.
A thin, tightly attached patch with a granular to minutely lobed surface, pale greenish to bluish-gray in color. The margins are irregular and slightly raised, forming a crust-like mat on the bark.

Irregular, diffuse white powdery patches cover the green leaf surfaces, giving them a frosted, dusty appearance. The fungal growth is fine, powdery, and patchy, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Fine, patchy white powder coats the upper surfaces of reddish, serrated leaves. The powdery growth appears diffuse and most prominent on the central and lower leaves, contrasting with the leaf’s natural coloration.
Slender green stems with small, rounded to oval leaves, many showing brown or necrotic edges and patchy discoloration. The plants are densely packed, with no distinct fungal fruiting bodies visible.

Resupinate, crust-like surface with wrinkled, convoluted texture in pale orange, peach, and cream hues. White, cottony mycelium is visible at the margins, and the surface is uneven with embedded dark debris.

Green leaves display pale yellowish discoloration and subtle vein clearing, with some areas appearing slightly wilted and patchy. Leaf surfaces are smooth with entire margins, and no distinct reproductive structures are visible.

Thin, irregular, blackish patches closely appressed to the wood surface, with diffuse, uneven margins and a matte to slightly rough texture. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible, and the growth forms elongated streaks along the branch.
Irregular, pale gray to whitish patches tightly attached to bark, with a rough, granular to slightly lobed surface and some powdery areas. Margins show small, leafy lobules.
Irregular, compact yellowish to ochre mass with a smooth, matte, slightly leathery surface. Margins are uneven and blend into the rough, dark woody substrate. No visible stalk or distinct sporangia.

Leaves display irregular, whitish, powdery patches with a fuzzy texture, forming a superficial coating on the upper surfaces. The affected areas contrast with the healthy green and yellowish leaves nearby.

Slender, upright, club-shaped fruiting body with a smooth, matte black surface and slightly irregular, wrinkled texture. The tip is rounded, and the stipe merges seamlessly with the head, both uniformly dark.

Numerous tiny, black, rounded to irregular glossy fruiting bodies scattered across a coarse, fibrous, light brown substrate with visible plant fragments. The fruiting bodies are minute, partially embedded, and lack prominent stalks, appearing directly attached to the substrate in an irregular distribution.

Large, convex caps with mottled pale yellow and pinkish tones, showing cracked, dry surfaces and irregular margins. Yellow flesh and pores bruise blue, while thick stems display reddish hues with yellow patches and blue staining. Surrounded by decaying leaves.
A small, pale gray to whitish patch with a foliose, lobed, and irregularly branched margin. The surface appears granular or powdery, and the thallus is tightly attached to the bark.

Irregular, diffuse white patches with a fine, powdery texture scattered across the green leaf surface. The colonies are slightly raised and superficial, lacking visible fruiting bodies or distinct structures.

A translucent, slender stalk rises vertically, ending in a rounded, bulbous tip. The surface is smooth with a few small nodular swellings along the stalk. The structure is unbranched and sharply defined against a blurred background.
Small, pale greenish to whitish leafy patches with irregularly branched, lobed margins. The surface appears granular to slightly powdery, forming scattered colonies on rough, cracked bark.

Numerous small, black, oval to slightly elongated fruiting bodies scattered irregularly across a pale, fibrous stem. The fruiting bodies are smooth, dark, and either embedded or slightly raised above the stem’s surface.

Pale, powdery whitish patches form irregular, slightly raised spots along the veins and surface of the green leaf. The fungal growth appears fine, granular, and patchy, contrasting with the smooth, elongated leaf.

Small, dark, irregularly oval fruiting bodies densely covered with long, stiff, radiating hair-like setae. The surface appears dark and subtly iridescent under magnification, with the setae giving a distinctly spiky outline. Fruiting bodies are solitary and separated.

Cup-shaped to irregularly lobed fruiting bodies with dark brown to nearly black inner surfaces and paler, roughened outer margins. Texture appears leathery and brittle, with visible cracking and uneven, wavy edges. Some fragments and a small patch of moss are present.

Thin, irregular ochre to yellowish-brown patch with a smooth surface and slightly granular margin. A small, dark central spot is present. The edges are diffuse, blending into the bark, and the form is flat and adherent.

Slender, orange to reddish-orange, filamentous structures emerge from decomposing leaf litter. The fungal elements are thin, elongated, wiry, and smooth, lacking any cap or expanded fruiting body, and are interwoven with the surrounding plant debris.
Numerous tiny, pale yellowish to off-white, globose bead-like structures densely scattered and clustered on a dark, moist wood surface, appearing gelatinous and moist.

A fine, powdery, whitish to pale gray coating covers the leaf surface, forming dense, irregular patches with a slightly fuzzy, granular texture. The fungal growth is most prominent along the central area, with no visible fruiting bodies.

Robust mushrooms with reddish-brown, cracked caps showing yellow patches. Bulbous yellowish stems display reddish mottling. Cut surfaces and pores stain vivid blue, contrasting with the yellow flesh. Texture appears moist and slightly rough.
A dense, white, powdery coating covers the upper surface of the green leaf, forming a continuous, slightly patchy layer that gives the leaf a matte appearance and obscures its natural texture.

Crustose surface with a granular to areolate texture, densely covered in small, black, rounded to slightly flattened bumps. The dark gray to black thallus appears rough and uneven, with fine cracks and irregularly grouped fruiting bodies.

Irregular, flattened patches with a yellowish to ochre hue, smooth to slightly granular texture, and uneven, lobed edges. Some areas display darker, fragmented sections, and the patches are spread contiguously along the moist, rough surface.
Elongated yellowish to brown streaks and linear lesions with dense, powdery rust-colored pustules breaking through the leaf surface, following the veins of the green leaves.

Yellowish to ochre, crust-like surface with an uneven, warty, and granular texture. The fruiting body shows maze-like patterns and subtle color variation, with denser, slightly raised patches scattered across the surface.
Numerous small, black, elongated to oval fruiting bodies are scattered irregularly along the slender, greenish-brown stem, appearing slightly raised and smooth against the lighter plant tissue.
Numerous small, dark brown to blackish powdery pustules densely clustered in irregular, linear streaks and patches on elongated green leaves, breaking through the leaf surface.

Small, rounded, gelatinous fruiting bodies with a yellow-orange hue, densely covered in greenish, wart-like granules. Surfaces appear moist, translucent, and bumpy, with irregular margins. The structures are clustered closely together.

Small, black, roughly spherical to irregular fruiting bodies clustered and partially embedded in decaying wood, with a rough, granular surface texture. The surrounding wood is pale with greenish discoloration.
A thin, whitish, powdery coating forms diffuse, irregular patches with a subtle, slightly fuzzy texture on the upper surface of the green leaf.
Numerous small, black, slightly raised spots are irregularly spaced along the length of the dry, pale stem. The dark, granular structures contrast sharply with the smooth, fibrous plant surface.
Numerous small, black, oval to elongated, slightly raised fruiting bodies are scattered across the smooth, pale tan stem, appearing glossy and embedded in the plant tissue.

Numerous small, dark brown to black, rounded pustules scattered across a green surface. The pustules are raised, irregularly distributed, and appear to rupture the surface, exposing granular, powdery spore masses. Surrounding tissue shows yellowing and browning.
Several pine cones in various stages of dark brown to blackish decomposition rest among dry, brown leaves. No distinct fungal fruiting bodies are visible on the cones or surrounding substrate.

Powdery, whitish to pale gray patches with a fine, granular texture cover the green surface. Irregularly shaped areas blend into the background, with scattered reddish-brown specks visible throughout the fungal growth.

Powdery, whitish patches form irregular, felt-like mats on a green surface. The texture is granular to powdery, with diffuse margins blending into the background and scattered brownish or reddish discoloration within the colony.

Small, irregular, gelatinous clusters with a yellowish to greenish hue, covered in minute, darker green warts. The moist, translucent fruiting bodies appear lobed and closely attached to the wood, forming scattered to gregarious groups.

Green, narrow leaves display a fine, whitish powdery coating in irregular patches, giving a silvery, dusty appearance. The powdery texture is diffuse and unevenly distributed across the upper leaf surfaces, with no distinct fruiting bodies visible.

Small, circular, dark structures embedded in rough, cracked bark, each with a central opening. The bark is mottled brown and green, with weathered, uneven texture and subtle raised areas around the fruiting bodies.

Slender, upright, orange to pale cylindrical structures with pointed tips emerge singly from decomposing leaves. The smooth, thin fruiting bodies stand out distinctly against the brown and tan leaf surface.
Irregular, yellowish patches with lobed margins and a matte, slightly powdery texture scattered across the dark, moist surface of decaying wood.

Irregular, yellowish-ochre mass with a cracked, crust-like surface, slightly raised from the dark, deeply fissured bark. The fruiting body appears brittle and dry, contrasting sharply with the rough, moist wood beneath.

Irregular, cushion-shaped ochre to yellow-brown mass with a smooth, cracked surface exposing a dark interior. The texture appears crustose and brittle, with clear fissures and a slightly raised margin.

A small, smooth, shiny, dark globose structure partially embedded in rough, cracked bark, surrounded by reddish-brown discoloration. Several tiny, circular, slightly raised spots are scattered nearby on the bark surface.

A pale gray to whitish patch with small, irregular, rounded lobes and a slightly wrinkled, granular surface. The margins are uneven and lobulate, forming a loosely attached, foliose cluster on rough bark.
A dense, powdery white mat of fine, filamentous hyphae spreads irregularly across the green leaf, with scattered minute yellowish dots and a cottony, superficial texture blending into the surface.
A fine, powdery, whitish to pale gray coating forms a dense, patchy, web-like layer on the green leaf surface, giving it a granular and unevenly distributed appearance.
Dense, irregular tufts of olive-green to dark brown fungal growth with a woolly, hairy texture. Fine, filamentous structures cover the surface, forming matted clumps scattered across the substrate.

Irregular, flattened yellowish to ochre patches scattered in small clusters along the dark, wet, deeply furrowed bark of a fallen log. The fruiting bodies have a smooth to slightly granular texture and stand out against the moist wood.

Small, black, roughly spherical to irregular fruiting bodies clustered and slightly raised above the bark, with a rough, granular texture. The structures are compact and embedded in the decayed, discolored wood surface.

A green leaf surface is coated with a dense, powdery, white to grayish layer. The fungal growth appears uniform, fine, and velvety, covering much of the leaf without visible fruiting bodies. The leaf margin is irregular and slightly damaged.

Irregular patch of pinkish, web-like mycelium with a cottony to slightly gelatinous texture, loosely interwoven among pale greenish lichen lobes and brown apothecia, creating a striking color and texture contrast.

Irregularly rounded, cushion-shaped mass with a smooth, matte, pale tan to light brown surface. The texture appears slightly powdery, with uneven edges blending into the wood. No stalk or distinct structures are visible.

Tiny, pale yellow to cream, cup-shaped to disc-like fruiting bodies with smooth, translucent surfaces, sparsely scattered on a dead stem. Each structure is minute, mostly less than a millimeter wide, and some have very short stalks.
Pale gray to whitish, loosely attached patches with small, irregularly lobed margins and a granular to slightly scaly surface, forming scattered colonies on rough, fissured bark.
Dense, powdery, white to off-white mycelial growth forms a patchy, irregular coating on the green surface, appearing as a fine, web-like or felted layer without visible fruiting bodies.

A compact, irregular mass with a woolly, matted texture and numerous dark, bristle-like hairs protruding from the surface. The coloration is a mix of dark brown to black with lighter yellowish-gray patches.
Small, circular, pale gray to whitish patch with short, rounded, overlapping lobes and a slightly ruffled, granular surface, lying flat against the bark.

Numerous tiny, white, rounded to slightly irregular dots are scattered across dark, fibrous, rough cone scales. The fruiting bodies are minute and lack visible stalks, standing out against the brown textured background.

A dark, nearly black, elongated and somewhat flattened structure with a matte, slightly roughened surface. Subtle longitudinal ridges and irregularities are visible, with a dry appearance and indistinct margins. The shape is linear and unbranched.

Dark, roughly spherical to ovoid body with irregular, spiky or filamentous projections radiating from the surface. Margins are uneven and fringed, giving a coarse, textured silhouette against a plain background.

Numerous delicate, dark, hair-like stalks each topped with a small, smooth, spherical black head. The thin stalks are straight to slightly curved, and the globose heads are evenly spaced, creating a pin-mold appearance.
Irregularly rounded, flattened fruiting body with a dry, yellowish-ochre surface. The texture appears slightly cracked, featuring several dark, almost black patches or openings on the outer layer.

A crust-like surface tightly attached to rock, covered with numerous small, black, rounded to irregular discs. The background is grayish and granular, with patches of lighter and darker tones. The discs are unevenly scattered and slightly raised above the thallus.

Dark, rounded fungal bodies with several prominent, stiff, hair-like setae radiating outward. The compact structures have a granular surface and are scattered across a pale background, each measuring around 200–350 micrometers.

Tiny, translucent to pale yellowish cup- or disc-shaped fruiting bodies on slender stalks, scattered across a rough, decomposed stem. The margins are smooth and the texture appears gelatinous or waxy.

Dense, dark brown to nearly black granular surface dotted with numerous tiny, white to pale reflective specks. The texture appears uneven and crustose, with an irregular margin sharply contrasting against the pale wood substrate. Fine structures dominate the millimeter-scale view.
Pale gray-green, patchy mat with small, irregular, flattened lobes. Surface appears slightly powdery or granular, with uneven, dissected margins forming dense, contiguous colonies on rough bark.

Large, thick mushrooms with cracked, mottled caps in reddish and yellowish tones. The cut flesh and upper stipe show a striking blue staining, while the pores and lower stipe are yellow with reddish markings. Cap margin is irregular and lobed.

Irregular, wedge-shaped section with a dense, dark, powdery interior and granular texture. Surrounded by a thin, pale outer layer, with crumbly, loose spore material scattered nearby. The margins are rough and uneven.

Pale greenish to whitish patch with a granular, uneven surface and indistinct, irregular margins blending into the tree bark. The colony appears crusty and patchy, lacking visible reproductive structures.

Pale cream to off-white, crust-like surface with a finely granular to warty texture. The surface appears uneven, slightly cracked, and undulating, with no visible fruiting bodies or pores. Margin is not clearly defined in this close-up view.

Large, robust fruiting body with a moist, cracked pinkish-red cap showing patches of discoloration and debris. The cap margin is irregular and eroded. Underside pores are yellowish with a reddish edge. Thick, bulbous stipe is reddish with yellow patches.

Green leaf with scattered, irregularly shaped pale lesions and necrotic spots, some with dark margins. Several holes and areas of tissue loss are visible, with lesions distributed across the leaf surface and prominent vein network.
Pale gray to whitish patch with a granular, powdery surface. Irregular, slightly lobed margins with some upturned edges. Closely appressed to the bark, forming a crust-like appearance.
A green leaf with a sharply defined, irregular yellow lesion containing a dense cluster of dark brown to black, powdery pustules breaking through the surface. No large fruiting bodies are visible.
