A dense, powdery white mat covers the green leaf surface, scattered with numerous tiny, dark, spherical structures embedded within the fungal growth. The infected area has an irregular margin.

Whitish, powdery coating forms diffuse, irregular patches on the upper surfaces of elongated green leaves, giving them a velvety, dusty texture. The fungal growth is most apparent along the veins and margins, blending subtly with the leaf surface.

Small, irregular whitish to pale gray patches scattered across a brown, textured surface. The patches appear powdery or granular and are closely appressed, lacking distinct margins or visible structures.

Dark, irregularly shaped, slightly raised patches with rough, granular surfaces and lighter central spots scattered across an orange-brown woody background. Margins blend into the substrate, and the patches appear somewhat confluent.

Reddish-brown surface densely covered with numerous small, rounded, slightly raised pustules. The texture appears rough and granular, with the pustules distributed irregularly across the area. No large fruiting bodies or spore masses are visible in this close-up view.

Clusters of medium-sized mushrooms with smooth, moist, convex caps in rich reddish-brown to yellowish-brown hues. One upturned cap reveals a yellowish underside. The caps are even-margined and partially obscured by dense green moss, grasses, and purple-flowered heather.

Three mushrooms with smooth, moist, pale lilac to grayish convex caps, closely spaced pale lilac gills, and sturdy cylindrical stipes tinged lilac, with soil clinging to the bases. Cap margins are even, and the fruiting bodies are arranged close together.

Numerous tiny, black, star-shaped or angular fruiting bodies scattered and loosely clustered on pale, weathered wood. The structures are slightly raised, irregular, and lack visible stalks, contrasting sharply with the substrate.

A compact, irregular blackish mass with a rough, warty surface. Small, rounded, shiny projections dot the surface. The grouping is dense, margins uneven, and the fungus is closely appressed to the wood.

Numerous minute, black, irregularly shaped and rough-textured structures scattered and loosely clustered across pale, weathered wood. Some areas show denser aggregations, while others are sparsely distributed, with the dark fruiting bodies contrasting against the substrate.

Clustered mushrooms with thick, pale to ochre caps displaying a cracked, scaly texture. Stipes are robust and soil-stained. The gills are a vivid deep violet-purple, contrasting sharply with the lighter cap and stem surfaces.

Numerous small, dark brown to blackish, slightly raised pustules are scattered irregularly across the green leaf surface, often concentrated along the veins and margins. The spots have a fine, powdery appearance.

Elongated, blackish, slightly raised patches are embedded along the length of a tan, dry conifer needle. The dark linear fruiting bodies have irregular margins and contrast with the lighter needle surface.

Minute, shallow, disc-like structures are scattered and embedded in the fibrous, decaying wood. The wood shows pale and greenish hues, with the fungal bodies appearing as tiny, inconspicuous depressions blending into the surface.
Numerous tiny, shallow, yellowish to orange disc-like structures with smooth surfaces and slightly sunken centers are scattered irregularly across the fibrous, partially decomposed wood.
A single, delicate, hair-like stalk rises from a granular greenish surface, topped with a tiny, dark, rounded head. The structure is minute and solitary, sharply focused against a blurred background.

Small, black, star-shaped or irregularly lobed fruiting bodies scattered on wood, appearing tough, shiny, and rough-textured. The dark structures are embedded in the substrate and contrast sharply with the lighter wood surface.

Minute, nearly circular to irregular dark fruiting bodies embedded in pale wood, each with a black margin and a lighter, granular center. The structures appear slightly sunken and scattered, with fine debris and filamentous material nearby.

Two globose, dark brown to blackish fruiting bodies with a rough, granular surface and subtle iridescent sheen, closely grouped and attached directly to a pale substrate. Margins are rounded and well-defined, with no visible stalks.

Yellowed, dry pine needles with elongated, black, slightly raised linear spots and patches scattered along their length. Fine, thread-like debris is attached to some needles, and the background is pale and featureless.

Numerous tiny, black, star-shaped fruiting bodies with sharply angular margins are scattered across the wood surface, appearing slightly raised or embedded. Their dark color and distinctive stellate form contrast with the lighter background.

Yellowish-brown to orange-brown cap with a sticky, moist surface and slightly inrolled margin. Cylindrical, robust stipe covered in fibrillose remnants, matching the cap in color. Partially obscured by grass and moss.

Brown and green conifer needles with elongated, black, linear, slightly raised and slit-like fruiting bodies embedded along their length. The fruiting bodies appear as dark, sunken lines or spots on the smooth needle surfaces.

Numerous tiny, rounded sporangia densely clustered along a stem, each with a brown interior and a frosted, white, net-like or crystalline surface, giving a granular, delicate appearance. Margins are irregular and sporangia are closely packed, measuring about 1 mm across.
A large, upright section of dead tree trunk with partially intact rough bark and exposed, weathered wood in brown and gray tones. No distinct fungal fruiting bodies are visible on the surface.

Small, black, disc-shaped to slightly cup-like fruiting bodies scattered and partially embedded in rough, reddish-brown bark. The fruiting bodies are mostly flush with or slightly raised above the wood surface, contrasting sharply with the substrate.

Pale greenish, crust-like surface with a cracked, areolate texture. The thallus appears granular to slightly powdery, forming irregular, patchy areas with indistinct margins blending into the background.

A dense, powdery white coating covers the upper surface of the green leaf, creating a fine, flour-like layer. The mycelium is most prominent along the veins, giving the leaf a frosted, dusted appearance.
A dense, powdery white mat covers the leaf surface, interspersed with numerous tiny, dark, dot-like structures scattered across the pale area.
Green stem marked by elongated, irregular dark blotches with reddish margins. The lesions appear slightly sunken and are distributed along the length of the stem, lacking visible fruiting bodies.

Upright, slender, pale greenish-gray stalks with a granular surface, some topped with small brownish cups or flattened tips. The base forms a crusty, lobed mat closely attached to the wood, with scattered, low-growing clusters.

Numerous small, black, star-shaped to irregularly lobed fruiting bodies with a tough, carbonaceous texture are scattered and closely grouped on a pale, fibrous wood surface. Margins are well-defined and some fruiting bodies overlap.

Numerous closely packed, nearly spherical fruiting bodies with dark brown to black coloration and a fine, granular or powdery surface. Each sphere is coated with a whitish or silvery sheen, giving a frosted appearance. The fruiting bodies are uniform in size and have rounded margins.

Crustose, granular green thallus with scattered, upright, tiny dark brown to blackish pin-like fruiting bodies on slender stalks. Rounded heads and delicate stalks are visible among uneven, patchy green, brown, and pale surfaces, with fine hyphal threads and a powdery texture.
A large section of tree trunk with bark removed, revealing pale, rough wood marked by numerous small holes and an uneven surface. No distinct fruiting bodies are visible.

Numerous tiny, rounded, orange to reddish-orange spots densely scattered across a yellowish-brown surface, creating a speckled pattern. The fruiting bodies are minute, smooth, and directly embedded without visible stalks.

Numerous tiny, dark, rounded to slightly irregular dots scattered across a pale, striated stem surface. The black, minute fruiting bodies are slightly raised and distributed singly or in loose groups, contrasting with the tan background.

Crustose, granular mat with a bumpy, uneven texture; densely packed, small, rounded, dark purplish-brown to blackish granules create a rough, nodular surface. Irregular margins blend into the substrate, with occasional greenish patches and lighter brown areas.

Clustered, globose to subglobose fruiting bodies with dark brown to purplish coloration, densely coated in fine, whitish, powdery or crystalline deposits. The surface appears granular and slightly rough, with no visible stalks in the close-up view.

Small, dark, rounded to irregular fruiting bodies scattered and partially embedded in glossy reddish-brown bark, some with a central pale spot. The bark shows slight peeling and the fungal structures appear as raised blackish spots.

A single, narrowly elliptical, black, shiny fruiting body about 1.23 mm long with a smooth surface, central longitudinal slit, and well-defined margins. The body is slightly curved and lies on a pale, linear substrate.

A close-up of a needle cross-section reveals a tan interior with a few small, black, elongated, slightly raised structures embedded near the surface. The needle appears dry and smooth, with sparse distribution of the dark fungal bodies.
Dark, oval to irregular fruiting bodies with rough, granular surfaces are closely grouped and partially embedded in the woody substrate, blending indistinctly into the surrounding wood.
Numerous tiny, blackish-green, star-shaped fruiting bodies scattered and loosely clustered on a pale woody surface. The structures are slightly raised, angular, and have a rough, irregular texture.
Small, black, disc-shaped fruiting bodies scattered across reddish-brown bark, each slightly raised with smooth, well-defined margins and a matte to subtly rough surface.

Numerous slender, upright black structures composed of small, glossy, bead-like segments arranged in linear chains along thin stems. The sporangia are smooth, shiny, and closely grouped, emerging among green grass blades.
Small, rounded, darkly pigmented fruiting bodies are scattered and slightly raised on the glossy surface of a woody twig, appearing as subtle bumps.

Numerous tiny, brown, rounded heads sit atop slender dark stalks, scattered across a rough, greenish and pale crusty surface. The heads appear granular or powdery, with some fruiting bodies solitary and others loosely clustered.

Small, dark, rounded to irregular structures scattered and slightly raised on the bark, each with a central pore. The stromata are dark brown to black, contrasting with the reddish-brown woody surface, and have a rough, granular texture.

Smooth, convex caps with a rich brown, slightly glossy surface. One mushroom shows a yellow pore layer underneath. Stems are robust and pale, with some soil at the base. Clustered among fine grasses and small flowering plants.

Elongated, dark, almost blackish, slightly sunken lesions with irregular, diffuse margins appear on a greenish to reddish stem covered in sharp thorns. The dark patches blend into the surrounding tissue, with no visible fruiting bodies.

A woody stem displays a darkened, nearly black patch with numerous tiny, raised black dots scattered along the bark. The affected area sharply transitions from healthy greenish bark to the darkened region, with the dots concentrated in the darker zone.

Numerous slender, upright, dark sporangia densely clustered among grass blades, each covered in small, rounded, bead-like structures. The elongated, cylindrical fruiting bodies have a rough, granular surface and a glistening, moist appearance.
Irregular, crust-like patch tightly attached to bark, pale yellowish in color with a granular to powdery texture and diffuse, uneven margins. No visible fruiting bodies.

Numerous small, pale whitish to grayish, circular to oval fruiting bodies scattered across the woody surface. These flat to slightly raised, button-like structures have a powdery to granular texture, some with faint central depressions, and are closely attached to the substrate.

Reddish-brown discoloration on stem with numerous tiny, pale to yellowish, slightly raised spots scattered across the surface. The affected area is irregularly shaped, blending into green tissue, and appears slightly rougher with fine hair-like structures.

Small, black, rounded to slightly conical fruiting bodies scattered across rough, reddish-brown bark. The structures are embedded or slightly raised, with a glossy surface amid patches of greenish lichen or moss.

Small to medium mushrooms with convex to bell-shaped brown caps, fibrous and slightly scaly surfaces, and faintly striate, uneven margins. Gills are closely spaced and pale, attached to slender, pale, fibrous stems with slightly bulbous bases.

A tightly adherent, crust-like patch with a pale yellowish to greenish hue. The surface is granular to slightly warty, uneven, and cracked at the margins, forming a rough, continuous texture without visible fruiting bodies.

Small, black, hard fruiting bodies with a shiny surface, each distinctly three-lobed or star-shaped, scattered and crowded on the wood. Margins are well-defined and slightly raised, giving a ridged appearance.

Small, black, oval to irregular fruiting bodies with rough surfaces are partially embedded in a fibrous, brown substrate. Some fruiting bodies appear slightly raised, contrasting against the textured woody background.
Numerous tiny, dark, dot-like structures are scattered irregularly along the dry, slender pieces of wood. These structures are embedded or slightly raised, giving the wood a speckled appearance.

Small, nearly spherical fruiting body with a smooth to finely granular surface, pale off-white to light brown in color, measuring just over 2 cm in diameter. No visible stalk or pores; sits directly on the ground.

Convex brown cap with a smooth, slightly sticky surface and lighter margin. Underside shows a yellowish pore layer. Cylindrical stem is yellow at the base, brownish above, with possible veil remnants.

Upright, slender, pale greenish-gray stalks with a granular surface, some topped by small, brownish, irregularly margined cup-shaped structures. Others are simple or branched, emerging from a crusty base on wood.
A dense layer of fine, powdery white growth covers the green leaf surface, dotted with numerous tiny, dark, spherical structures scattered throughout.

Granular, greenish crust covers an uneven surface, dotted with numerous minute, dark brown to blackish pin-like fruiting bodies on slender stalks with rounded heads. Fine hyphal threads are visible among the rough, uneven texture.
Branch surface densely covered with small, dark, slightly raised, irregular fruiting bodies embedded in reddish-brown bark, interspersed with whitish patches, giving a rough, pitted texture.

Medium-sized mushroom with a pale, slightly curved stipe showing faint purplish tones near the closely spaced, grayish to purplish gills. The stipe base is covered in soil and debris, and the cap margin is rounded and smooth.
Numerous small, shallow, tan to light brown disc-like structures with smooth surfaces and thin, slightly raised margins are scattered and partially sunken into the pale, weathered wood surface.

A dark brown to black, elongated streak with slightly sunken, irregular margins runs along the woody stem, contrasting sharply with the surrounding greenish-brown bark. No visible fruiting bodies are present.

Small, pale green to grayish patches scattered across decaying wood, appearing crustose to squamulose with granular or powdery texture. No prominent upright structures are visible; the patches are irregularly distributed on the wood surface.
